documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text:
The culture and arts sector in Wales is at a crucial point, and the future now looks very vulnerable indeed. In the meantime, national museums across the globe are transforming into more interactive spaces, which are driven by technology, to engage with new audiences. For example, the Smithsonian has used podcasting successfully to bring history and culture to audiences beyond their physical sites. The Louvre has partnered with Snapchat to develop innovative interpretation equipment for six of its sections. And the V&A East museum has held a late-night programme, bringing together DJ residencies, temporary bars and access to exhibitions after hours. 

So, Minister, what support is the Welsh Government providing to assist museums and other cultural organisations in Wales to modernise, so that they are relevant, accessible and competitive in an age that is increasingly digital and experience led? And what else can the Welsh Government do to help museums to attract new audiences, and to attract younger audiences too?
documents.text_cy:
Mae sector diwylliant a chelfyddydau Cymru mewn cyfnod hollbwysig, ac mae’r dyfodol ar hyn o bryd yn edrych yn fregus iawn. Yn y cyfamser, mae amgueddfeydd cenedlaethol ledled y byd yn trawsnewid yn ofodau mwy rhyngweithiol, sy’n cael eu gyrru gan dechnoleg i ymgysylltu â chynulleidfaoedd newydd. Er enghraifft, mae’r Smithsonian wedi defnyddio podlediadau yn llwyddiannus i ddod â hanes a diwylliant i gynulleidfaoedd y tu hwnt i’w safleoedd ffisegol nhw. Mae’r Louvre wedi partneru â Snapchat i ddefnyddio offer dehongli arloesol ar gyfer chwech o’i hadrannau. Ac mae amgueddfa dwyrain V&A wedi cynnal rhaglen hwyrnos, sy’n dod â phreswylfeydd DJ, bariau dros dro, a mynediad i arddangosfeydd ar ôl oriau ynghyd.

Felly, Weinidog, pa gefnogaeth mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei darparu i helpu amgueddfeydd a sefydliadau diwylliannol yng Nghymru i foderneiddio, fel eu bod yn berthnasol, yn hygyrch ac yn gystadleuol mewn oes sy’n gynyddol ddigidol ac sy’n cael ei arwain gan brofiad? A beth arall y gall Llywodraeth Cymru ei wneud i helpu amgueddfeydd i ddenu cynulleidfaoedd newydd, a denu cynulleidfaoedd iau hefyd?

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text:
I think you are very likely to receive an invitation shortly from Amgueddfa Cymru to go to some their late-night events. I haven't attended any of those myself, but they have been doing these for quite a while now, and it's been great to see that cross-section of ages as these spaces become live at a time of night when I'm usually in bed, unfortunately. But there is very innovative work going on. 

I have seen excellent examples of this across Wales. There have been examples of being able to stay overnight in some of our museums and so on, with your children, a night at the museum—not quite like the film, but that kind of atmosphere. So, I don't want to give the impression that we are not innovating here in Wales. Do I believe that there are more opportunities we could pursue? Yes. Do I believe that through our new culture and sport strategy it is necessary that digital is more prominent? Yes, I certainly do.

So, I think that we need to build on the innovative work that's happening, looking at the kind of things that we could be doing here in Wales. And by bringing the creative industries into that culture strategy, I think there is also an opportunity to develop partnerships between the creative industries and our cultural institutions, and that that is part of the strategy for the economy as well. So, there are opportunities to do more, but there is already innovation going on. We need to see more of that, and more investment in the strategy underlying it.
documents.text_cy:
Dwi’n meddwl y byddwch chi yn debygol iawn rŵan o dderbyn gwahoddiad gan Amgueddfa Cymru i fynychu rhai o’u digwyddiadau hwyrnos nhw. Dwi heb fynychu fy hun, ond mae nhw eisoes wedi bod yn gwneud hyn, ac mae wedi bod yn wych gweld y croesdoriad o oedrannau wrth i’r gofodau hyn ddod yn fyw ar adeg o’r nos pan dwi fel arfer yn fy ngwely erbyn hyn, yn anffodus. Ond mae yna waith arloesol yn digwydd.

Dwi wedi gweld esiamplau gwych o hyn ledled Cymru. Mae yna esiamplau wedi bod o allu aros dros nos yn rhai o’n hamgueddfeydd ni ac ati, efo’ch plant, night at the museum—ddim cweit fel y ffilm, ond y math yna o awyrgylch. Felly, dwi ddim eisiau rhoi'r argraff nad ydyn ni'n arloesi yma yng Nghymru. Ydw i’n credu bod yna fwy o gyfleoedd? Ydw. Ydw i’n credu, drwy’r strategaeth diwylliant a chwaraeon, ei bod hi’n angenrheidiol bod digidol yn fwy amlwg? Ydw, yn sicr.

Felly, dwi’n meddwl bod angen adeiladu ar y gwaith arloesol sy’n digwydd, ac edrych ar y math o bethau y gallem ni fod yn eu gwneud yma yng Nghymru. Trwy ddod â’r diwydiannau creadigol yn rhan o’r strategaeth ddiwylliant, dwi’n meddwl bod yna gyfle hefyd i ddatblygu partneriaethau rhwng y diwydiannau creadigol a’n sefydliadau diwylliannol ni, a bod hwnna’n rhan o’r strategaeth o ran yr economi hefyd. Felly, mae yna gyfleoedd i wneud mwy, ond mae yna arloesi eisoes yn digwydd. Mae eisiau gweld mwy ohono fo, a mwy o fuddsoddi yn y strategaeth y tu ôl i hynny.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: This is central to our vision for the culture and sport strategy. In our first 100 days in Government, we commissioned an investigation into sports facilities across Wales, and through Sport Wales, we are investing in affordable local opportunities, supporting community clubs to improve facilities, with targeted action to reach those who face the greatest barriers to participation.
documents.text_cy: Mae hyn yn ganolog i’n gweledigaeth ni ar gyfer y strategaeth diwylliant a chwaraeon newydd. Yn ein 100 diwrnod cyntaf mewn Llywodraeth, fe wnaethom ni gomisiynu archwiliad i gyfleusterau chwaraeon ledled Cymru, a thrwy Chwaraeon Cymru, mi rydyn ni’n buddsoddi mewn cyfleoedd lleol sydd yn fforddiadwy, yn cefnogi clybiau cymunedol i wella cyfleusterau, gyda gweithredu wedi’i dargedu i gyrraedd y rhai sy’n wynebu’r rhwystrau mwyaf o ran cyfranogiad.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text:
Diolch, Drefnydd. In Blaenau Gwent, 49 per cent of children experience income deprivation—that's the highest proportion of any local authority in Wales. Meanwhile, in Caerphilly borough, Cefn Fforest leisure centre has had its hours reduced, with local reports highlighting a massive decline in visits compared to before the change. Behind every lost visit, as we know, is a child disengaging from sport, a missed opportunity and potential left unfulfilled.

Families in deprived communities can't always travel to the next leisure centre, particularly in areas with limited cross-valley transport links. We know that sport improves physical and mental well-being, builds confidence and opens doors for young people. So, what specific investment can Blaenau Gwent, Rhymney and Caerphilly expect, and will you prioritise maintaining vital existing facilities in the deprived communities, rather than directing further investment towards areas that are already better served? Diolch.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text:
I have been clear since taking post that we do want to ensure equal access for everyone in Wales, and that we do recognise the barriers that currently exist—barriers that I have to work on a cross-portfolio basis to overcome. I’m pleased that Mark Hooper is here—we’ve had a number of discussions in relation to the role that transport plays in allowing access to opportunities and facilities. I know through my own casework of a number of families who have been in touch with me to say that if they don't have a car, just how challenging it is for their children to be part of a football or rugby team, because they can't get to games on the weekends. Fewer clubs can afford to get minibuses, where they may have done so in the past. These are challenges and there are no overnight solutions.

There is investment taking place through the community facilities programme in Blaenau Gwent and also through Sport Wales in Caerphilly. I do think that what we need to look at is that if we are investing in facilities, how then can we support people to overcome the other barriers preventing them from participating. There are excellent programmes in Caerphilly, such as Let's Go Girls, which is an excellent example where they can provide support. But in looking at the culture and sport strategy more broadly, I'm eager to hear directly from young people and from families about the challenges that they're currently experiencing, and I would encourage all Senedd Members to contribute ideas to what would make a difference to your constituents.
documents.text_cy:
Dwi wedi bod yn glir ers dod yn Weinidog ein bod ni eisiau sicrhau mynediad cydradd i bawb yng Nghymru, a’n bod ni yn cydnabod y rhwystrau sy’n bodoli ar y funud—rhwystrau y mae’n rhaid i fi weithio ar sail trawsbortffolio i'w goresgyn. Dwi’n falch bod Mark Hooper yma rŵan—rydyn ni wedi cael amryw o drafodaethau o ran y rôl mae trafnidiaeth yn ei chwarae o ran galluogi mynediad neu atal mynediad at gyfleusterau a chyfleoedd. Dwi'n gwybod drwy waith achos fy hun am amryw o deuluoedd sydd wedi cysylltu efo fi i ddweud os nad oes ganddyn nhw gar, pa mor heriol ydy o i'w plant nhw fod yn rhan o dîm pêl-droed neu rygbi, oherwydd eu bod nhw'n methu eu cael i gemau ar benwythnosau, gyda llai o glybiau'n gallu fforddio cael bws mini, lle oedd ganddyn nhw yn y gorffennol. Mae'r rhain yn heriau ac nid oes datrysiadau dros nos chwaith.

Mae yna fuddsoddiad yn digwydd drwy'r rhaglen cyfleusterau cymunedol ym Mlaenau Gwent a hefyd drwy Chwaraeon Cymru yng Nghaerffili. Dwi'n meddwl mai'r hyn rydyn ni angen edrych arno fo ydy os ydyn ni'n buddsoddi mewn cyfleusterau, sut wedyn ydyn ni'n cefnogi pobl i oresgyn y rhwystrau eraill sy'n eu hatal nhw rhag cyfranogi. Mae yna raglenni gwych yng Nghaerffili, megis Let's Go Girls, sy'n esiampl wych lle maen nhw'n gallu cefnogi hynny. Ond fel rhan o edrych ar strategaeth diwylliant a chwaraeon, dwi'n awyddus iawn i glywed yn uniongyrchol gan bobl ifanc a chan deuluoedd am yr heriau y maen nhw'n eu profi rŵan, a byddwn i'n annog pob Aelod o'r Senedd i gyfrannu syniadau at yr hyn a fyddai'n gwneud gwahaniaeth i'ch etholwyr chi.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: In Cardiff, affordable indoor sport provision is essential given our reputation as a rainy city, yet rising court and hall hire costs are increasingly pricing out grass-roots clubs and working-class families. At the same time, it took 10 years of campaigning and partnership working between Basketball Wales and Cardiff Council to secure refurbishment of the outdoor courts at Roath Pleasure Gardens—a project that's going to be a genuine game-changer for the local community. Whilst investment in facilities is welcome, many young people still face financial barriers to participation. So, what specific action is the Welsh Government taking to support grass-roots clubs and ensure that a young person's opportunity to play sport is determined by their talent and ambition, not their postcode or their parents' ability to cough up?

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text:
Thank you. That's the very work that we're doing now by working on a cross-portfolio basis. The fact that we have committed to ensuring, through the new child poverty strategy, that culture, sport and participation in those is a central part of that work is important. The fact in the past has been that that hasn't been a sufficient factor. We all know of the barriers in place. We all know that the participation gap is widening, reliant on family income, and that's not how it should be. So, I am asking you all, Members who have examples of projects that are truly making a difference, where do you think we should be focusing our resources. Please share those with us as we develop a strategy that truly will tackle these challenges.

I agree that there are excellent pockets of practice in Cardiff and in different parts of Wales, but, often, pilot schemes come to an end, although we know that they work. I do want to ensure, if there is a pilot, that we then look as to whether there is funding available to continue with that work. There are also some projects where sponsorship comes in and some businesses who can provide more into the community, that that is targeted and supported in order to allow those projects to proceed. I don't have all of the solutions in terms of 'how' at the moment, but this is part of the work we're undertaking.
documents.text_cy:
Diolch. Dyna'r union waith rydyn ni yn ei wneud rŵan drwy weithio'n drawsbortffolio. Mae'r ffaith ein bod ni wedi ymrwymo i sicrhau, drwy'r strategaeth tlodi plant newydd, fod diwylliant, chwaraeon a'r cyfranogiad at y rheini'n rhan ganolog o'r gwaith yn bwysig. Dwi'n meddwl bod y ffaith wedi bod yn y gorffennol efallai nad yw hynny wedi bod yn ddigon o ffactor. Rydyn ni i gyd yn gwybod am y rhwystrau sydd yna. Rydyn ni'n gwybod bod y bwlch o ran cyfranogiad yn cynyddu yn ddibynnol ar incwm teuluol, ac nid dyna sut y dylai hi fod. Felly, dwi'n gofyn i chi, yr holl Aelodau sydd efo esiamplau o brosiectau sy'n gwneud gwahaniaeth, lle ydych chi'n meddwl y dylen ni fod yn canolbwyntio'r adnoddau, i rannu hynny efo ni wrth inni ddatblygu strategaeth sydd wirioneddol yn mynd i fynd i'r afael efo'r heriau hyn. 

Dwi'n cytuno bod yna bocedi gwych o waith yn digwydd yng Nghaerdydd ac mewn gwahanol lefydd o Gymru, ond, yn aml, mae rhai cynlluniau peilota yn dod i ben, er ein bod ni'n gwybod eu bod nhw'n gweithio. Dwi eisiau sicrhau, os oes yna beilot, ein bod ni'n edrych ar a oes yna gyllid ar gael i barhau efo'r gwaith hwnnw. Mae yna hefyd rai cynlluniau lle mae yna nawdd yn dod i mewn, lle mae rhai busnesau sydd efo incwm ac yn gallu rhoi mwy o fudd i mewn i'r gymuned, bod hwnnw wedyn yn cael ei dargedu a'i gefnogi er mwyn caniatáu cynlluniau o'r fath. Does gen i ddim o'r holl atebion o ran 'sut' ar y funud, ond mae hwn yn rhan o'r gwaith rydyn ni'n ei wneud.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text:
Participating in sport brings many benefits, as we all know. It provides physical health, mental health and well-being, while also providing opportunities to build community and bring people together. But barriers to participation can prevent people from accessing these benefits altogether. Sport Wales's 'State of the Nation' report for 2024-25 notes that two of the three factors most likely to encourage future participation in sport are if there were more facilities, clubs or groups in their area, and if it cost less.

There are pockets in my constituency of Caerdydd Ffynnon Taf, more specifically in Cardiff east, where public transport is infrequent and expensive. And with the decline in youth centres and community facilities in recent years following cuts, it feels as though this problem is only getting worse. I appreciate you've already answered part of this question, but I wanted to ask what action is being taken to measure and address transport-related barriers specifically, and how you're working with the Deputy Minister for Transport to make sure that there is participation for low-income families.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: Thank you. As I said, these are ongoing conversations. The fact that we have the Deputy First Minister leading on child poverty, the fact that we have Mark Hooper leading on transport, that you have me, and that we also have Nerys Evans, who is looking at the preventative health aspect and public health aspects, all working on this in order to ensure that the plans that we put in place do tackle these challenges, I hope can give you an assurance that we all understand the role that we have to play. I'm not just standing here saying, 'This is a problem for transport', but what we're trying to work together on is the solutions and on how we can make it more affordable. Because, at the end of the day, if people can't access sport and can't participate, then, ultimately, they're going to cost more to the health service, be that because of mental health or physical health. That preventative side is crucially important, but I do recognise that these challenges are very real at present. We're not going to change this overnight, but we do have to move to a preventative agenda here in Wales, and that is this Government's commitment.
documents.text_cy: Diolch. Fel roeddwn i'n ei ddweud, mae'r rhain yn sgyrsiau byw iawn. Mae'r ffaith bod gyda ni Ddirprwy Brif Weinidog sydd yn arwain ar dlodi plant, bod gyda ni Mark Hooper sydd yn arwain ar drafnidiaeth, bod gyda chi fi, bod gennym ni Nerys Evans, sydd yn edrych o ran yr ochr iechyd ataliol ac iechyd cyhoeddus, yn cydweithio ar hyn er mwyn sicrhau bod y cynlluniau rydyn ni'n eu rhoi yn mynd i'r afael â'r heriau yma, gobeithio yn rhoi'r sicrwydd i chi ein bod ni i gyd yn gweld y rôl sydd gennym ni i'w chwarae. Dwi ddim jest yma'n sefyll yn dweud, 'Mae hon yn broblem i drafnidiaeth', ond beth dŷn ni'n trio cydweithio arno fo ydy, 'Beth ydy'r datrysiadau hynny? Sut ydyn ni'n ei wneud o'n fwy fforddiadwy?' Oherwydd, ar ddiwedd y dydd, os nad ydy pobl yn cael mynediad at chwaraeon a'n gallu cyfranogi, yna maen nhw'n mynd i gostio mwy o arian i'r gwasanaeth iechyd yn y pen draw, boed hynny o ran iechyd meddwl neu iechyd corfforol. Mae'r ochr ataliol yn allweddol bwysig, ond dwi yn cydnabod bod yr heriau hyn yn real ar y funud. Dŷn ni ddim yn mynd i newid hyn dros nos, ond mae'n rhaid inni symud at agenda ataliol yma yng Nghymru, a dyna'r ymrwymiad sydd gan y Llywodraeth hon.
