documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text:
Minister, the programme for government commits to prioritising equality of access to sport for people of all ages, backgrounds and abilities, as well as increasing participation and improving grass-roots facilities. Back in June, I had the opportunity to visit the Margam Stags inclusion football festival, bringing together children and young people of different ages and abilities. The Margam Football Club Inclusion Stags are well known in my constituency for the invaluable opportunities they provide for people who might otherwise face significant barriers to taking part in sport.

I also recently visited Afan United's brand-new facilities in Sandfields, where a major investment has transformed the site into a high-quality community football hub. This has put modern sporting facilities right on the doorstep of a community where levels of deprivation are high. These are the kinds of projects that can make equality of access a reality and give young people opportunities they might not otherwise have had. Minister, how will the Government ensure that its commitment to improve grass-roots facilities is targeted towards those communities and groups where barriers to participation are greatest?

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text:
I thank the Member for that supplementary question. It's great to hear about the important projects that are currently proceeding, and one of the things that I hope that you and other Members will do, through that call for evidence, is to provide those examples where this is happening. It's not something that can happen in the future, it is already happening in our communities. But there is a risk that, without investment, that work won't continue, and also, as you mentioned, that there is an inequality of access, because if you don't have that group, then you don't have an opportunity to participate. 

So, it's important that we learn from those examples that work, and then we look at how that can be duplicated in a way that works for that community, because all communities will be different in terms of solutions. But certainly, that's the kind of evidence that we are gathering at the moment. I'm always willing to visit any examples; I am opening myself up to further invitations here.

But it is also important that we highlight the opportunities that already exist, because some people simply aren't aware of what's available in their communities. So, there is a role for us too to be using our platforms in order to share that information. There is more that we can do too through things like social prescribing in order to encourage those who find it difficult, even when that kind of facility or provision is available locally.
documents.text_cy:
Diolch i'r Aelod am y cwestiwn ychwanegol hwnnw. Mae'n wych clywed am y prosiectau pwysig yma sydd yn digwydd rŵan, ac un o'r pethau dwi'n gobeithio y byddwch chi ac Aelodau eraill yn ei wneud, drwy'r alwad am dystiolaeth, ydy gyrru esiamplau lle mae hyn yn digwydd. Dydy o ddim yn rhywbeth a all ddigwydd yn y dyfodol, mae o'n digwydd yn ein cymunedau ni rŵan. Ond mae yna risg, heb fuddsoddiad, na fydd y gwaith hwnnw'n ddigwydd, a hefyd, fel dŷch chi wedi sôn, fod yna anghyfartaledd, oherwydd os nad ydych chi efo'r grŵp hwnnw, yna does yna ddim cyfle i gyfranogi.

Felly, mae'n bwysig ein bod ni'n dysgu o'r esiamplau hynny sydd yn gweithio a'n bod ni'n edrych wedyn ar sut mae hynny'n dyblygu ac yn dyblygu mewn ffordd sydd yn gweithio i'r gymuned honno, oherwydd mi fydd pob cymuned yn wahanol o ran y datrysiadau. Ond yn sicr, dyna'r math o dystiolaeth dŷn ni'n ei chasglu ar y funud. Dwi wastad yn barod iawn i ymweld efo unrhyw esiamplau hefyd; dwi'n agor fy hun i fyny am wahoddiadau pellach.

Ond mae'n bwysig hefyd ein bod ni'n uwcholeuo'r cyfleoedd sydd eisoes yn bodoli, oherwydd nid yw rhai pobl yn gwybod beth sydd ar gael yn eu cymunedau nhw. Felly, mae yna rôl i ni i gyd hefyd fod yn defnyddio'r platfformau sydd gennym ni i rannu'r wybodaeth honno. Mae yna fwy y medrwn ni ei wneud hefyd drwy bethau fel social prescribing i fod yn annog y rheini sydd yn dal i'w chael hi'n anodd, hyd yn oed pan mae'r math yna o gyfleuster ar gael yn lleol.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: Diolch, Deputy Llywydd. Cabinet Minister, accessible sport means good facilities close to home, with affordable, fair access to every club, school and girls' team. I welcome your expansion support for artificial pitches. In May 2024, the then Cabinet Secretary told this Chamber that the Rhondda third generation facility was a Welsh Rugby Union priority, with Coleg y Cymoedd identified as a potential solution. She urged partners to work towards applying in the following financial year. More than two years on, our community needs a clear route forward. Will you confirm whether an application has been submitted for that proposal, and whether this year's funding could support a modern fourth generation all-weather rugby pitch that meets the required standards for training and competitive matches while the Sport Wales audit proceeds? Diolch.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: Thank you for your question. I don't know, but I will endeavour to find out what the situation is. You will also appreciate that it was a different party and a different Minister that gave that response at that time, but I'm happy to follow up and ensure you receive that response.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: 5. What is the Welsh Government doing to promote the growth of esports in Wales? OQ64683
documents.text_cy: 5. Beth mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei wneud i hyrwyddo twf e-chwaraeon yng Nghymru? OQ64683

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: Creative Wales have supported Esports Wales to develop skills and creative career pathways linked to esports. We actively consider proposals for economic investment in esports as they arise, and we continue to support Wales’s wider video games industry through development and production funding, skills programmes and trade opportunities. For example, in September we took a delegation of eight Welsh games developers to the Tokyo Game Show. But as you heard in my response to Mike Hedges earlier on today, there is more that I believe we could be doing, and we will be looking into this as we develop a new strategy.
documents.text_cy: Mae Cymru Greadigol wedi cefnogi Esports Wales i ddatblygu sgiliau a llwybrau gyrfaol creadigol sy'n gysylltiedig ag e-chwaraeon. Rydyn ni'n ystyried cynigion ar gyfer buddsoddiad economaidd mewn e-chwaraeon wrth iddynt godi, a dŷn ni'n parhau i gefnogi diwydiant gemau fideo ehangach Cymru drwy gyllid datblygu a chynhyrchu, rhaglenni sgiliau a chyfleoedd masnach. Er enghraifft, ym mis Medi mi aethon ni â dirprwyaeth o wyth o ddatblygwyr gemau o Gymru i'r Tokyo Game Show. Ond fel clywsoch chi yn fy ymateb i Mike Hedges yn gynharach, mae yna fwy, dwi'n credu, y gallem ni fod yn ei wneud, a byddwn ni'n edrych ar hwn fel datblygiad strategaeth newydd.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: Thank you. Esports is something that I'm deeply passionate about, and I didn't expect, before coming down to the Chamber today, to be beaten to the post by the Labour spokesman on this issue, but I'm glad that it has happened. One area that I'd like to talk about is the benefits that esports events could bring to Wales. Stockton University in the United States described esports tournaments and events as 'the untapped tourism opportunity'. The Greater London Authority recently estimated that a single esports event, the 2025 BLAST Premier London Open, generated more than £30 million of economic impact for the city. Now, the mayor of London has recently set out an ambition to put London at the heart of global esports, and I see no reason why we shouldn't have a similar ambition here in Wales so that we can enjoy the benefits of this growing industry. So, will you commit today to take positive action to help attract more esports events to Wales? Diolch.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: Thank you for the question. I believe that there's a new cross-party group going to be set up on esports. We have two parties here who have already committed to that, and hopefully the assurance I've given you that I recognise that we could be doing more in terms of esports in Wales—. I agree with that, and I am very keen to hear ideas from any Members in terms of how we could incorporate that within a new strategy.
documents.text_cy: Diolch am y cwestiwn. Dwi'n credu bod yna grŵp trawsbleidiol newydd yn mynd i gael ei ddechrau ar esports. Mae gennym ni ddwy blaid eisoes wedi ymrwymo i hynny, a gobeithio bod y sicrwydd dwi wedi ei roi fy mod i'n cydnabod y gallem ni fod yn gwneud mwy o ran esports yng Nghymru—. Dwi'n cytuno efo hynny, a dwi'n awyddus iawn i glywed syniadau gan unrhyw Aelodau o ran sut y byddem ni'n gallu ymgorffori hynny o fewn strategaeth newydd.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: 6. Will the Cabinet Minister provide an update on the new national school swimming and water safety programme? OQ64701
documents.text_cy: 6. A wnaiff y Gweinidog Cabinet roi diweddariad ar y rhaglen genedlaethol newydd nofio a diogelwch dŵr i ysgolion? OQ64701

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: I thank the Member. Nofio Ysgol is our new national school swimming and water safety programme, providing pupils in years 4 and 5 with a consistent national offer of at least 20 swimming and water safety lessons. This work began in nine local authorities in September, marking the first phase of a planned Wales-wide roll-out.
documents.text_cy: Diolch i'r Aelod. Mae Nofio Ysgol yn rhaglen genedlaethol newydd ar gyfer nofio a diogelwch dŵr ysgolion, sy'n darparu cynnig cenedlaethol cyson o o leiaf 20 o wersi nofio a diogelwch dŵr i ddisgyblion blynyddoedd 4 a 5. Mi ddechreuodd y gwaith hwn mewn naw awdurdod lleol yn barod ym mis Medi, gan nodi cam cyntaf y cyflwyniad fydd wedyn ledled Cymru.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: Learning to swim is one of the best gifts you can give a child. I have had the privilege of swimming in the Hampstead Heath ponds, the Serpentine, Lake Bled, off the Isle of Skye and a good deal of the west coast, and one day I'm going to do a swimathon again. It is a skill that you can keep for life, takes you to places you would never dream of and takes you around the world. But not every child has the benefit of that kind of start. Swim Wales found that only 42 per cent of children in years 3 to 6 could swim 25m unaided, which is a serious figure for a country with our coastline, and it's also a safety issue. So, I welcome this programme, but could the Cabinet Minister please outline how it will get to grips with teaching children in areas where there is little provision or where the pools have closed down, as free lessons are not much use if there's no place to have them?

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text:
Thank you. That is exactly why we are looking at facilities across Wales, and that is why we are starting with nine local authorities in different parts of Wales—some rural, where swimming pools have closed down—to understand those challenges and to understand how we prioritise investment. We do know at the moment that only 13 per cent of children under 11 do take swimming lessons on an extracurricular basis. We also know that there are thousands of children that leave primary school every year being unable to swim.

It is a skill that can save lives. It's a skill that can keep you active throughout your life as well, because it's one of the few sports that you can do at any age. So, that is why we are committed to this, and it was wonderful to see, at a recent visit with the First Minister, these lessons being provided, and seeing even those children who could already swim developing their skills in terms of saving lives and what to do in a position if they were to fall into water unexpectedly or in facilities where the water is very cold, so that they understood the dangers. It's not just a matter of learning to swim, but learning life-saving skills too.
documents.text_cy:
Diolch. Dyna yn union pam dŷn ni'n edrych ar gyfleusterau ledled Cymru hefyd, a dyna pam dŷn ni'n dechrau efo naw awdurdod lleol sydd mewn gwahanol rannau o Gymru—rhai yn wledig, lle mae yna byllau nofio wedi cau—i ddeall yr heriau hynny a deall sut dŷn ni'n blaenoriaethu buddsoddiad. Dŷn ni yn gwybod ar y funud mai dim ond 13 y cant o blant dan 11 oed sy'n cymryd gwersi nofio allgyrsiol. Dŷn ni hefyd yn gwybod bod yna filoedd o blant yn gadael ysgol gynradd bob blwyddyn sy'n methu â nofio.

Mae hi yn sgìl sy'n gallu achub bywyd. Mae hi yn sgìl sy'n gallu eich cadw chi'n actif drwy gydol eich oes, oherwydd mae'n un o'r unig chwaraeon dŷch chi yn gallu eu gwneud dim ots pa oed ydych chi hefyd. Felly, dyna pam dŷn ni wedi ymrwymo i hyn, ac mi oedd o'n wych gweld, mewn ymweliad diweddar gyda'r Prif Weinidog, y gwersi hyn ar waith, a gweld hyd yn oed y plant hynny oedd yn gallu nofio yn datblygu eu sgiliau o ran achub bywyd a hefyd beth i wneud mewn sefyllfa os oedden nhw'n disgyn i'r dŵr heb rybudd neu mewn cyfleusterau lle mae'r dŵr yn oer iawn neu i ddeall y peryglon. Dydy o ddim jest yn fater o ddysgu pobl i nofio, ond dysgu'r sgiliau all arbed bywyd hefyd.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: 7. Will the Cabinet Minister provide an update on the Sport Wales audit of regional and community sports facilities? OQ64715
documents.text_cy: 7. A wnaiff y Gweinidog Cabinet roi diweddariad ar archwiliad Chwaraeon Cymru o gyfleusterau chwaraeon rhanbarthol a chymunedol? OQ64715

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: I thank the Member. This work is going ahead, reviewing the information held by governing bodies, local authorities and other partners to build a national picture of community, regional and national sports facilities across Wales. This initial work will start by identifying gaps in the evidence and developing options for presenting and maintaining the data, helping to inform future strategic capital investment.
documents.text_cy: Diolch i'r Aelod. Mae'r gwaith hwn yn mynd rhagddo yn adolygu'r wybodaeth sy'n cael ei gadw gan gyrff llywodraethu, awdurdodau lleol a phartneriaid eraill i greu darlun cenedlaethol o gyfleusterau chwaraeon cymunedol, rhanbarthol a chenedlaethol ledled Cymru. Mae'r gwaith cychwynnol hwn yn dechrau nodi bylchau yn y dystiolaeth ac yn datblygu opsiynau ar gyfer cyflwyno a chynnal y data, gan helpu i lywio buddsoddiad cyfalaf mwy strategol yn y dyfodol.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: Cefn Fforest Leisure Centre remains open, but Caerphilly council significantly reduced its opening hours in 2025 and closed the fitness suite. Will the Sport Wales data capture include changes to opening hours, the facility availability at each site and the distance to alternative provision, so that the future capital investment reflects the level of provision communities have access to?

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: The initial phase is looking at the sites. We are also looking at what additional data is available, including on opening hours and so forth. What's difficult at the moment is that we don't have a full picture in order to be able to understand what the barriers are and what are the things that could change and where investment would make that difference. So, that work is going ahead, and I will ensure that I have raised with Sport Wales what you've raised today, to ensure that opening hours form part of that, so that we can try and see the fullest possible picture. There are challenges, because some local authorities hold this data, but we know that a lot of local authorities also have outsourced some of these services, so it is difficult to access that data in some cases, but we are trying to get the fullest possible picture.
documents.text_cy: Mae'r cam cyntaf yn edrych ar y lleoliadau. Dŷn ni hefyd yn edrych ar ba ddata ychwanegol sydd ar gael, gan gynnwys oriau agor ac ati. Yr hyn sydd yn anodd ar y funud ydy bod gennym ni ddim darlun llawn er mwyn deall beth ydy'r rhwystrau a beth ydy'r pethau all newid a lle byddai buddsoddiad yn neud y gwahaniaeth. Felly, mae'r gwaith hwnnw'n mynd rhagddo ac mi fyddaf i'n sicrhau fy mod i wedi codi efo Chwaraeon Cymru yr hyn dŷch chi wedi ei godi heddiw, i sicrhau bod oriau agor yn rhan o hynny, er mwyn inni allu gweld y darlun mwyaf llawn posibl. Mae yna heriau, oherwydd mae rhai awdurdodau lleol efo'r data hwn, ond dŷn ni'n gwybod bod lot o awdurdodau lleol hefyd wedi 'outsource-io' rhai o'r gwasanaethau hyn, felly mae o yn anodd cael at y data, ond dŷn ni yn trio cael darlun mor llawn ag sy'n bosibl.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: Thank you. The final question, Minister, question 8, Safa Elhassan.
documents.text_cy: Diolch. A'r cwestiwn olaf, Weinidog, cwestiwn 8, Safa Elhassan.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: 8. What action is the Welsh Government taking to improve access to cultural, sporting and recreational activities in Gŵyr Abertawe? OQ64707
documents.text_cy: 8. Pa gamau mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i wella mynediad at weithgareddau diwylliannol, chwaraeon a hamdden yng Ngŵyr Abertawe? OQ64707

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: The Welsh Government, and myself as Minister, are committed to ensuring that culture and sport are accessible to everyone. he work on developing a new culture and sport strategy for Wales is enabling us to look at how we can support that aim. Through the call for evidence, we want to hear from people in communities across Wales, including in Gŵyr Abertawe, ensuring that a broad range of voices and experiences helps shape how culture, the arts and sport are accessed and experienced.
documents.text_cy: Mae Llywodraeth Cymru, a minnau fel Gweinidog, wedi ymrwymo i sicrhau bod diwylliant a chwaraeon yn hygyrch i bawb. Drwy'r gwaith ar ddatblygu strategaeth diwylliant a chwaraeon, rydyn ni'n edrych ar sut y gallwn ni gefnogi'r nod hwnnw. Drwy'r alwad am dystiolaeth, dŷn ni eisiau clywed gan bobl ledled Cymru, gan gynnwys yng Ngŵyr Abertawe, er mwyn sicrhau bod ystod eang o leisiau a phrofiadau yn llywio'r modd mae pobl yn cael mynediad at ddiwylliant, y celfyddydau a chwaraeon.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text:
Diolch, Minister. On a recent visit to Sketty Youth Club, alongside the Cabinet Secretary for Education and the Welsh Language, I saw first-hand how a welcoming community centre can bring children, parents and grandparents together through outdoor activities. Groups such as Sketty Tea Lounge 50-plus club also show how important it is to create opportunities for older people to stay active, connected and engaged.

In Swansea bay, the HARBWR project provides another excellent example, using creative and cultural activities to support people experiencing loneliness and poor mental health. As a clinician, I know that prevention starts long before someone reaches a hospital or a GP surgery.

How will the culture and sports strategy help bring community organisations and health services together, so that more people across Gŵyr Abertawe can benefit from affordable cultural and recreational activities to improve well-being and help prevent ill health?

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text:
I thank the Member. It's wonderful to hear about the excellent things happening in your constituency, and I do enjoy hearing of these examples. That's why it is so important that all of us do contribute these ideas and these examples to the development of the strategy, so that we seek to ensure that consistency. I do hope that the commitment that you've heard from me again today, commitments that you've heard from the Cabinet Minister for health and the two Deputy Ministers on health, also does demonstrate that we are working together on this issue.

I've had enough, and I've said regularly, having read reports that say that Wales needs to move towards a preventative agenda, that that work has to start, and it has started. It will take time to change systems, but we have to do it. We know that culture and sports do have a positive impact on physical and mental health, so the work we're doing now is to look at how we can ensure that all of the systems that have operated in silos can concord, and that we can get the potential of culture and sport delivered in terms of health, in terms of the economy and in terms of the future of our nation.
documents.text_cy:
Diolch i'r Aelod. Mae'n wych clywed am y pethau rhagorol sydd yn digwydd yn eich etholaeth chi, a dwi wir yn mwynhau clywed am yr esiamplau hyn. Dyna pam y mae o yn bwysig bod pawb ohonon ni yn cyfrannu y syniadau hyn a'r enghreifftiau hyn i ddatblygiad y strategaeth, fel ein bod ni'n edrych ar sicrhau'r cysondeb hwnnw. Dwi'n gobeithio bod yr ymrwymiad dŷch chi wedi'i glywed gen i eto heddiw, ymrwymiadau dŷch chi wedi eu clywed gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros iechyd a'r ddwy Ddirprwy Weinidogion o ran iechyd, hefyd yn dangos ein bod ni yn gweithio ar y cyd o ran y mater yma.

Dwi wedi cael llond bol, a dwi wedi dweud yn rheolaidd, o ddarllen adroddiadau sydd yn dweud bod angen i Gymru symud at agenda ataliol, fod yn rhaid i'r gwaith hwnnw ddechrau, ac mae'r gwaith hwnnw wedi dechrau. Mae'n mynd i gymryd amser i newid y systemau, ond mae'n rhaid i ni ei wneud. Dŷn ni'n gwybod bod diwylliant a chwaraeon yn cael effaith gadarnhaol ar iechyd corfforol ac iechyd meddyliol, felly y gwaith dŷn ni'n ei wneud rŵan ydy ar sut dŷn ni'n sicrhau bod yr holl systemau sydd wedi gweithredu ar wahân yn cyd-fynd, a'n bod ni'n gallu cael potensial diwylliant a chwaraeon wedi'i wireddu o ran iechyd, o ran yr economi ac o ran dyfodol ein cenedl.

documents.item: 1. Questions to the Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
documents.text: Thank you very much, Minister.
documents.text_cy: Diolch yn fawr iawn i chi, Weinidog.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: We'll move on now to questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance. Question 1—Rebeca Phillips.
documents.text_cy: Ymlaen i gwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid. Cwestiwn 1—Rebeca Phillips.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: 1. Will the Cabinet Minister provide an update on the review of the local government funding formula? OQ64711
documents.text_cy: 1. A wnaiff y Gweinidog Cabinet ddarparu diweddariad ar adolygiad o'r fformiwla ariannu llywodraeth leol? OQ64711

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: The Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning is proceeding with the local government funding formula review in partnership with local authorities. This includes joint technical work with local government and independent research through the Wales Centre for Public Policy. We're expecting a report during the summer of 2027 on this work.
documents.text_cy: Mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio yn bwrw ymlaen â'r adolygiad o fformiwla ariannu llywodraeth leol mewn partneriaeth â llywodraeth leol. Mae hyn yn cynnwys gwaith technegol ar y cyd gyda llywodraeth leol ac ymchwil annibynnol drwy Ganolfan Polisi Cyhoeddus Cymru. Mae disgwyl adroddiad yn ystod haf 2027 ar y gwaith yma.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Thank you very much. As a former county councillor of 14 years, I welcome this Government's commitment to renewing the relationship between the Welsh Government and local authorities by ensuring that they are full partners in the design and the delivery of public services. Local authorities do excellent work across our communities, and we will rely on them to deliver many of this Government's priorities. It is therefore essential that the funding formula reflects the true cost of service delivery in different parts of Wales. Could the Minister therefore provide information on the discussions she has had with the Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning and with the Welsh Local Government Association regarding this matter? Thank you.
documents.text_cy: Diolch yn fawr. Fel cyn-gynghorydd sir o 14 o flynyddoedd, croesawaf ymrwymiad y Llywodraeth hon i adnewyddu'r berthynas rhwng Llywodraeth Cymru ac awdurdodau lleol drwy sicrhau eu bod nhw'n bartneriaid llawn yn nyluniad a darpariaeth gwasanaethau cyhoeddus. Mae awdurdodau lleol yn gwneud gwaith rhagorol ar draws ein cymunedau, a byddwn yn dibynnu arnynt i gyflawni llawer o flaenoriaethau'r Llywodraeth hon. Mae'n hanfodol felly fod y fformiwla ariannu yn adlewyrchu cost go iawn darparu gwasanaethau mewn gwahanol rannau o Gymru. A allai'r Gweinidog felly ddarparu gwybodaeth am ba drafodaethau mae hi wedi'u cael gyda'r Gweinidog Llywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio a Chymdeithas Llywodraeth Leol Cymru ynglŷn â'r mater yma? Diolch.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text:
Thank you for that supplementary question, and may I agree with the Member that county councils in Wales play a crucial role in delivering public services and play a crucial role in terms of how this Government will deliver its programme for government, and they play a key role, of course, in providing for and representing people at a local level? So, the funding of local government to allow them to deliver in that way is important in that regard.

Now, there was a question on the discussions that I've been having with the Minister for local government in terms of appropriate funding for local authorities—yes, certainly, that is happening as part of the discussions around the preparation of the annual budget for Wales. Last week, I believe, I met, along with the Minister for local government, with local authorities in the WLGA finance sub-group as we discussed the annual budget, and changes and the discussion around the funding formula too. So, that ongoing relationship and discussion with local government is very important to this Government in order to deliver all of the work that our county councils are responsible for doing.
documents.text_cy:
Diolch am y cwestiwn pellach yna, ac a gaf i gytuno gyda'r Aelod fod cynghorau sir yng Nghymru yn chwarae rhan allweddol o ran delifro gwasanaethau cyhoeddus ac yn chwarae rôl hanfodol o ran sut bydd y Llywodraeth yma'n gwireddu ein rhaglen lywodraethu ni, ac yn chwarae rhan allweddol, wrth gwrs, yn darparu a chynrychioli'r bobl yn lleol? Ac felly mae ariannu llywodraeth leol, i'w galluogi nhw i fedru cyflawni yn y modd yma, yn bwysig yn hynny o beth.

Cwestiwn ynglŷn â'r drafodaeth dwi wedi ei chael gyda'r Gweinidog llywodraeth leol o ran ariannu priodol ar gyfer awdurdodau lleol—ie, yn sicr, mae hynny'n digwydd fel rhan o'r drafodaeth ynglŷn â pharatoi ar gyfer cyllideb flynyddol Cymru. Ac, wythnos ddiwethaf dwi'n meddwl oedd hi, fe wnes i gwrdd, ar y cyd â'r Gweinidog llywodraeth leol, gydag awdurdodau lleol yn finance sub-group yr WLGA wrth i ni drafod y gyllideb flynyddol, ie, a newidiadau a'r drafodaeth ynglŷn â'r fformiwla cyllido hefyd. Felly, mae'r berthynas a'r drafodaeth barhaus yna gyda llywodraeth leol yn bwysig iawn i'r Llywodraeth yma er mwyn cyflawni'r holl waith mae'n cynghorau sir ni yn gyfrifol am ei wneud.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Cabinet Minister, whilst your colleague is in America deep-seeking the meaning of artificial intelligence, and the First Minister is running around Cardiff market, there are some very pressing challenges in Carmarthenshire affecting rural communities. Cash-strapped councils are being forced into short-term, penny-pinching false economies like threatening to close our small rural schools. In fact, two schools were closed today. Councils must manage their money, yes, I absolutely agree, but when will the Welsh Government prioritise ours? Will this funding formula finally direct real taxpayers' money to safeguard these small rural schools, the beating hearts of our communities? Diolch.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Well, the promotion of Wales overseas is an important aspect of the work that this Government wants to accomplish on behalf of businesses and communities in Wales. The First Minister was drinking a cup of coffee in a corridor as I passed him on the way down to the Chamber earlier, gallivanting nowhere at that point, hot coffee in his hand. Can I just say that, as I answered Rebeca earlier, local authorities provide a really key role in being able to deliver services—education, social services—in all our communities in Wales? They face tough, challenging budgetary situations, as we do as a national Government as well. Taking these decisions at a local level is important. We believe in the decentralisation of decision making in Wales, not setting arbitrary caps on local authorities in terms of the money that they have the ability to spend, as you will want to propose later on this afternoon. They have to take difficult decisions. I represent a constituency west of yours, also rural in nature. I've seen local schools at times have to be closed; I've seen campaigns to save local schools, and those local schools remain open today. These are complex decisions that local communities and their representatives have to take, and should not be trivialised in this place; they need to follow the processes, listen to the voices of those people involved, and take the right decisions. It's not for us to dictate the decisions that should be taken locally.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: The key drivers of demand on local authority budgets include population, school numbers, social care and deprivation. Any changes to the weighting of these indicators in the local government funding formula will have a huge impact on the ability of councils with the greatest population density and deprivation to deliver essential services. Following the Welsh Government's recent deviation from the established funding formula, councils with the highest levels of deprivation do need clarity. They need to know whether any lasting changes to the formula will come with any significant extra funding or will the funding pot still be the same.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text:
Thank you. You outline the challenges, of course, with the creation of a funding formula that works for all communities and all local authorities across Wales, as diverse as they are for us in Wales. The review that is now being undertaken, part of it in direct partnership and in collaboration with local government, the technical review, part of that is updating and recalibrating the formula while retaining its established needs-based methodology, and initial work that's currently ongoing is focused on some of the areas you've identified, and they are the main areas of local government delivery, and they are on education and personal social services.

As I said in my initial answer, then, this work is ongoing and it is in partnership with local authorities. The final report on this work will be next summer, and that will then decide how we move forward on these issues. I suspect we'll have many conversations around these issues both here, but, importantly, between ourselves as a Government and local government, which are the essential deliverers of so many aspects of our public services and need to be funded according to the need that they need to deliver in a variety of different circumstances.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: 2. What discussions has the Cabinet Minister had with HM Treasury and HMRC regarding the potential impact of the Welsh Government’s proposed Cynnal payments on recipients’ tax and benefits status? OQ64718
documents.text_cy: 2. Pa drafodaethau mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet wedi'u cael gyda Thrysorlys Ei Fawrhydi a Chyllid a Thollau ei Fawrhydi ynglŷn ag effaith bosibl taliadau arfaethedig Cynnal Llywodraeth Cymru ar statws treth a budd-daliadau y rhai sy'n ei gael? OQ64718

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: I have written to the Chancellor and Financial Secretary to the Treasury to request a tax exemption for Cynnal. I've also raised the issue in a meeting with the Chief Secretary to the Treasury. In discussions with the Minister of State in the Department for Work and Pensions, the Deputy First Minister has also requested that the payment be disregarded for benefits calculation purposes. I also welcome the Prime Minister's positive comments to explore these matters further.
documents.text_cy: Dwi wedi ysgrifennu at y Canghellor ac Ysgrifennydd Ariannol y Trysorlys i ofyn am esemptiad treth ar gyfer Cynnal. Dwi hefyd wedi codi'r mater mewn cyfarfod â Phrif Ysgrifennydd y Trysorlys. Mewn trafodaethau gyda'r Gweinidog Gwladol ar gyfer yr Adran Gwaith a Phensiynau, mae'r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog hefyd wedi gwneud cais i'r taliad gael ei ddiystyru at ddibenion cyfrifo budd-daliadau. Dwi'n croesawu hefyd, yn hyn o beth, sylwadau cadarnhaol Prif Weinidog newydd y Deyrnas Gyfunol o ran edrych ymhellach ar y materion yma.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Diolch. On average, across Wales, around one in three children live in poverty, with some of the most deprived wards found in Clwyd, which is where I represent. We often talk about food poverty and fuel poverty, but I want to draw the Siambr's attention to another less visible consequence of poverty, and that is bed poverty. Too many children are sleeping in broken or unsuitable beds, having to share beds or regularly sleeping on sofas, chairs or even floors because they simply cannot afford an adequate bed. Sleep deprivation can affect almost every major system of the body. The introduction of the Cynnal payment is obviously very welcome, but we must ensure that this does not affect other means-tested benefits. Furthermore, if we're serious about creating lasting change for children living in poverty, we need the powers to tackle that poverty ourselves. I understand from news sources that there's been some discussion around this, but will the Minister commit to not only continuing discussions with the relevant departments to ensure Cynnal payments do not affect means-tested benefits, but also to pressing the UK Government for the full devolution of welfare powers to Wales?

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Thank you. You outline in your question the real, debilitating impact of poverty on children in our communities, and that's why this Government is seeking to introduce a child poverty payment, direct payment, in the form of our Cynnal scheme. It will be very difficult for us as a Government to introduce that pilot if we are not given those exemptions to benefits by the UK Government, so we are pursuing vigorously a decision by the UK Government to exempt the Cynnal payment from any impact on benefits or taxes. So, we will be pursuing those. And I'm hoping, even in my letter to the UK Government, that this could be something the UK Government provides clarity on in the budget in April. And just to say, in terms of the full devolution of welfare—or progress on the devolution of welfare—then that is certainly something that the First Minister is pursuing as part of the need to see greater devolution. We've seen how the part devolution of welfare for Scotland has enabled a child poverty payment to be made in Scotland, and we are prevented from doing so at this point by some of the restrictions around our devolution settlement. So, we need to change that in order to help us with the work that we want to tackle in terms of child poverty.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text:
Minister, Labour rejected your supplementary budget in July. Mark Drakeford suggested that they should have accepted the deal. And now, Labour and Plaid have reached an agreement. The old band is back together, playing live on the stage of failed promises. [Interruption.] Your defeated budget proposed £2 million for Cynnal payments, but up to 15,000 children could be affected, and that would cost £7.8 million over a year before administration costs.

As recently as 7 October, you were still seeking safeguards from HM Revenue and Customs and the Department for Work and Pensions to prevent families losing out through tax or reduced benefits. It's good to hear your statement, but why on earth announce financial help before securing the protections needed to ensure recipients actually benefit? That looks short-sighted and publicity-seeking. Does this risk become another disingenuous Plaid manifesto promise scuppered by inadequate preparation and uncertainty over funding? Minister, does your agreement with Labour fund the financial support needed to deliver Cynnal from the first payment and beyond the original £2 million budget? Thank you.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: The Cynnal payment is no longer just a manifesto commitment, it is a pledge of the Government elected by the people of Wales in May. We've moved on from a manifesto, so keep up. The programme for government, of course, wants to implement and, across our work as a Government, tackle child poverty, for the clear reasons outlined by Becca in her earlier question. So, we need to be progressing this. We think that there are very straightforward measures that the UK Government could take to enable us to introduce this payment. Designing the Cynnal payment pilot, as it will be, continues as part of the work of this Government now, and, as I've already outlined, we'll be continuing discussions with the UK Government to enable us to bring it into action.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: I now call on the party spokespeople to question the Cabinet Minister. Reform UK spokesperson, Cai Parry-Jones.
documents.text_cy: Galwaf nawr ar lefarwyr y pleidiau i holi'r Gweinidog Cabinet. Llefarydd Reform UK, Cai Parry-Jones.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Thank you, Deputy Llywydd. Minister, on 15 September, your Government announced—fronted, I noticed, by the First Minister—that, to pay for rate cuts for smaller venues, it would raise the tax on Wales's largest business premises. Eight days later, Admiral, Wales's only FTSE 100 company, announced 500 job cuts, and Legal & General, which employs more than 2,000 people in Cardiff, announced 1,000 job cuts. Now, Admiral had already told the markets back in March that it had to find £100 million of savings. So, you knew some of our biggest employers were under pressure and you still decided to send them a bigger tax bill. Your impact assessment, released later, on 6 October, speculates about jobs that might be created in hospitality, but, crucially, it says nothing about the potential job losses for the businesses having to pay more. So, a simple question, Minister: will you publish a full assessment of the jobs impact of your tax rise before this Senedd is asked to vote on it—'yes' or 'no'?

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: I'm not aware of anything that those companies that have regrettably announced job losses have said that it is in any way as a result of the 30 per cent reduction in the business rates available to the leisure and hospitality industries in Wales. They are large companies and they will want to see a workforce that works for them in Wales, that are living in vibrant communities, vibrant city centres here in Cardiff. As part of providing for ensuring that we have the ability for smaller businesses to continue trading in our city centres and in our high streets, then this Government took the decision to reduce those business rates on the hospitality and leisure sectors. So, I hope that you will be supporting that, and any information that you believe I need to provide in order to facilitate your support for the reduction of business rates for our pubs and clubs, then I'd be happy to supply that for you.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Did the Minister answer the question?

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: I don't think so.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text:
No. Last week, the Deputy Minister for Transport told us that work on a third Menai crossing starts now, which is warm words, but my colleagues were right to ask where the money is, because Wales has been here before. The M4 relief road, originally promised in 1991, millions spent on planning and then scrapped, partly over funding issues. And, yes, the third crossing, originally promised in 2018, £3 million spent on planning and then scrapped, partly over funding issues. The current estimate for this project today is £670 million, yet only £20 million to £25 million has been budgeted over the next five years for it, and that's just been for planning.

We can see where this is going, Minister: you'll kick the big spending can down the road while you're in the job, a future finance Minister will announce we don't have enough money and then quietly shelve it. A sad transportation groundhog day. So, Minister, will you prove me wrong and pledge where the money to build the bridge will come from in this Senedd term?

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: This is most definitely not groundhog day for the Menai bridge. I would have said that last week was very much a first day of a big announcement by this Government on the future of a third Menai crossing. In Government, in this Senedd, when you have been here a longer time, you will know that large infrastructure projects take a long time to deliver. Therefore, if you don't start today and start the planning and fund the planning, as this Government is doing for the Menai bridge, then you will not get to that day when there is a third Menai bridge. So, you have to start and then you continue that work. This Government has started the process of designing the work that's needed to improve the resilience of the two bridges in place today and tackle the need for a third Menai crossing. We're committed to doing that work, to funding that work in its development phases, and, hopefully, both you and I will be here long enough to see that third Menai bridge built.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Minister, you've spent five months in this job. Let's look at your record: you're responsible for the first Welsh Government budget ever to be defeated in the history of devolution; you've twice managed to vote against your own Government, by mistake; you've had to correct the record for getting financial figures wrong in the Chamber; and, just now, you've failed to explain where the money's going to come from for the third Menai crossing. That is why I wasn't surprised that, when your Government needed to negotiate with my party for the next supplementary budget, it didn't send you, it sent the Minister for Government effectiveness. I have a source saying the exact same thing happened with the Labour negotiations. The First Minister said he had learnt lessons over the summer. The lesson, it appears, is to sideline you. So, Minister, who is actually running the Welsh Government's finances? And given it clearly isn't you, is it not time to officially hand over the reins to someone more competent?

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text:
When you've been here 27 years and you've only managed to vote wrong twice, then maybe I can come back to you and see what your record will be like in 27 years. Look, you can trivialise these spokespeople questions if you want to. There are really important questions that could be asked at this point, and you've asked whether it's Dafydd Trystan or myself that turned up to a meeting with you. I am the Minister for finance. There are others in this Government who will also be negotiating with people across this Senedd, both on funding and on legislation. We do not work as a silo in this Government; we work as a team. I don't know how you work within Reform—I'd love an insight into that. But, as a Government, we are committed to working with you and with all parties here to secure Senedd support for a budget that enables public services to be delivered in Wales.

It is easy to sit on a Reform bench, or even a Tory bench, and always vote 'no'. The difficult bit of this work, you will find, is to find—[Interruption.] I apologise for dragging another political party into this. I shouldn't have done that, and I was trivialising at that point. You will find, in the work of forging co-operation and ensuring the need to pass budgets and pass legislation in this place—because ultimately that is why we are voted to this place by the people of Wales—that you need to talk across political parties and within political parties, and that's what I'll continue to do.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Welsh Labour spokesperson, Huw Thomas.
documents.text_cy: Llefarydd Llafur Cymru, Huw Thomas.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Thanks, Dirprwy Lywydd. May I wish you both a happy shwmae? Minister, as we've already heard, the major news this week was the agreement on the supplementary budget. May I thank you personally for your meetings with me and the fact that we've been able to come positively to an agreement that ensures £60 million additionally for schools and colleges for additional learning needs? This is a victory. I visited a school in Pentrebane in Cardiff west this morning. It's obviously going to make a huge difference that that funding is going to come through immediately now.
documents.text_cy: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. A gaf i ddymuno shwmae hapus i'r ddwy ohonoch chi? Weinidog, fel rydym ni wedi clywed, newyddion mawr yr wythnos yma oedd y cytundeb ar y gyllideb atodol. A gaf i ddiolch i chi yn bersonol am eich cyfarfodydd gyda fi a'r ffaith ein bod ni wedi gallu dod yn gadarnhaol at gytundeb sydd yn sicrhau £60 miliwn ychwanegol i ysgolion a cholegau ar gyfer anghenion dysgu ychwanegol? Mae hyn yn fuddugoliaeth. Bues i'n ymweld ag ysgol ym Mhentrebane yng ngorllewin Caerdydd y bore yma. Mae'n amlwg yn mynd i wneud gwahaniaeth bod yr arian yn dod yn syth yn awr.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: We are clear that this money is an important down payment, but it's not enough. Further funding is required. You have spoken previously about your concerns about in-year overspends within the NHS and so the need to hold money back, unallocated, to address that concern. I accept that as a prudent argument at the moment, but what are you doing to drive those overspends down? In a written question answer to me—

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Huw, can you conclude, please?

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: If I can just put this across. A month or two ago, the net annual deficit forecast for health boards was £333 million. What is that figure now? Have you managed to get that figure down, so that we can unlock additional funding for schools and colleges?

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Shwmae. Shwmae to the whole Chamber this afternoon. It was important that we came to an agreement and that there will, hopefully, now be a majority in this Chamber to allow that expenditure on additional learning needs, which needs that £60 million that will be voted on in the next few weeks, so that that important funding reaches our schools and colleges in order to ensure that the pressure our schools are currently under is alleviated somewhat. I know that you believe that more funding is required, and some follow-up to that funding in future, and that's something that this Chamber as a whole will need to discuss as we bring forward the budget for next year.
documents.text_cy: Shwmae. Shwmae i'r Siambr gyfan y prynhawn yma. Mi oedd yn bwysig ein bod ni'n dod i gytundeb a bod yna fwyafrif, gobeithio, yn mynd i fod yn y Siambr yma nawr i ganiatáu'r gwariant ar gyfer anghenion dysgu ychwanegol, sydd angen y £60 miliwn yna a fydd yn cael ei bleidleisio arno yn yr wythnosau nesaf yma, fel bod yr arian pwysig yna yn cyrraedd ein hysgolion ni a'n colegau ni er mwyn sicrhau bod y pwysau y mae ein hysgolion ni oddi tano nawr yn cael ei leddfu rhyw gymaint. Dwi'n gwybod eich bod chi'n credu bod angen mwy o arian yn hynny o beth, a dilyniant i'r arian hynny, ac mae hwnna'n rhywbeth bydd y Siambr yma yn ei chyfanrwydd angen ei drafod wrth inni gyflwyno'r gyllideb ar gyfer y flwyddyn nesaf.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: In reference to the particular challenges within the NHS and in financial control within the NHS, this is an issue that I am continuing to have conversations on with the health department and the health Minister. We do need to ensure that we get to a situation where we are confident at the start of a financial year that the NHS is able to live within the means of the budget that it's been allocated for that year. There is considerable inflation within the NHS—in public services in general, but particularly in the NHS—and that is once again because it's in the wider economy and that is a challenge to our NHS budget management. These are issues that we continue to need to grapple with and they have very real life consequences for people out there who receive services from the NHS.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Thanks. I didn't hear a figure there of what the overspend had declined by, so perhaps we could correspond by letter on that. One of your priorities as a Government is the childcare offer. One of our priorities is to ensure fair pay in the economy.
documents.text_cy: Diolch. Wnes i ddim clywed ffigur yn fanna o beth roedd y gorwariant wedi gostwng ganddo, felly efallai gallwn chi ysgrifennu drwy lythyr ar y mater. Un o'ch blaenoriaethau chi fel Llywodraeth ydy'r cynnig gofal plant. Un o'n blaenoriaethau ni ydy sicrhau tâl teg yn yr economi.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Welsh Labour's manifesto made a commitment to ensuring that businesses receiving Welsh Government support pay the real living wage. I've asked previously whether businesses funded through the childcare offer will be mandated to pay the real living wage. I've not had a clear answer on that yet, but I note your programme for government commits you to adopting a 'fair work first' approach to public sector grants, loans and contracts. I wonder what progress have you made in putting that commitment into practice. Specifically, will payment of the real living wage become a condition of public sector contracts and financial support to businesses? And what is the timetable for introducing those requirements? Diolch yn fawr.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text:
On the current position, in terms of the NHS position within the financial year, I'm happy to write to you further on the exact position as we are in month 6 or 7 of the financial year.

It is our commitment as a Government to ensure that there is fair pay for fair work and we are looking to embed that across our work as a Government, whether that is in the wages available to people who undertake contracts for the Welsh public sector, but also in terms of the question that you pose in particular there, the grants available to businesses. So, I'll need to take that particular part of the question away and write to you to confirm on that one what the intention of the economy Minister is on that particular aspect of the question.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Welsh Conservatives' spokesperson, Sam Rowlands.
documents.text_cy: Llefarydd y Ceidwadwyr Cymreig, Sam Rowlands.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Thank you, Deputy Presiding Officer. Cabinet Minister, in May of this year, Plaid Cymru stood on a platform of change. Of course, we've seen in 2007 the One Wales coalition that Plaid Cymru had with Labour for a four-year period; in 2021, there was the co-operation agreement that Plaid Cymru had with Labour throughout that term; in 2025, the budget deal between Plaid Cymru and Labour for this next financial year again. And of course, yesterday, you announced a deal with Welsh Labour for the supplementary budget again. I wonder how this signals a platform of change that Plaid Cymru stood on in May.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text:
Interesting for me, this analysis of who works with who, because if we think about the supplementary budget and if we think of how that supplementary budget will progress its way through the Senedd, then it may well be that it's supported by one or two political parties here. It may be that it's allowed through by another political party, but it may be voted against by another cosy consensus between Reform and the Tories here. Alliances work in different ways in this place. I'm always keen to look to see how we create new alliances. I'm always keen to work with political parties across this Chamber. You know, I love it when the whole Chamber works together as one, but that doesn't seem to be the pattern of the day these days.

So, this Government has a programme for government for the next four years. It is a programme of change. A budget will be announced in the next few weeks that will enable that programme to move up a gear. We are a Government of change. That programme is the first programme for government that is not a Labour programme for government. That is change in itself and it will do different things.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text:
Thank you, Cabinet Minister. I'm sure you can appreciate that when you say it's a Government of change, but continuing the same alliances that have taken place many times during the 27 years of this Senedd, it's hard for the electorate to understand how those two things can be true at once. And of course, during that campaign, you claimed that the economic plan would unlock potential, support good jobs and grow businesses, and in forming a new Welsh Government, many people hoped for a shift away from 27 years of working with Labour in one way or another. Instead, we see that deal being done again.

In particular, around the issue around additional learning needs, it's absolutely right that funding has been allocated to those children with additional learning needs. But a single-year assessment is not enough to provide schools, teachers, parents and learners with the certainty that they desperately need. The National Association of Head Teachers have told us that this deal falls significantly short of ALN's identified need in Wales. The Welsh Labour leader himself said yesterday that the ALN sector needed long-term sustainability. It baffles the mind as to why a long-term deal, therefore, wasn't agreed to. So, I wonder if you believe, in your heart of hearts, that the Plaid Cymru and Labour supplementary budget deal will bring the change that Wales needs, does do enough to expand support for ALN learners, and will help grow the economy across the whole of Wales.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Well, that supplementary budget is, of course, much more than just the £60 million of additional funding for additional learning needs. That in itself is important and is an addition to the budget that was discussed here in the summer, and that's an important contribution that will now go directly to schools and colleges in Wales. It won't go as a result of you voting against the supplementary budget, or Reform possibly voting against the supplementary budget. It'll go because Plaid Cymru will vote for that supplementary budget, and Labour will allow that supplementary budget to pass. It is because of our actions that it will go, not your actions. So, that is a contribution that will make a difference to young people in Wales, and just continually voting against delivers nothing.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: 3. What assessment has the Welsh Government made of the impact of the land transaction tax since its introduction in 2018? OQ64688
documents.text_cy: 3. Pa asesiad mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi'i wneud o effaith y dreth trafodiadau tir ers ei chyflwyno yn 2018? OQ64688

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Land transaction tax has made a significant contribution to the Welsh budget since its introduction in 2018. It's provided over £2.5 billion for vital public services and infrastructure in Wales.
documents.text_cy: Mae'r dreth trafodiadau tir wedi gwneud cyfraniad sylweddol i gyllideb Cymru ers ei chyflwyno yn 2018. Mae wedi sicrhau cyllid gwerth dros £2.5 biliwn ar gyfer gwasanaethau cyhoeddus a seilwaith hanfodol yng Nghymru.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: I refer to my register of interests. I want to focus on two areas of concern, Minister. First is our first-time buyers. There is no first-time buyer relief in Wales. So, for example, if a first-time buyer buys a £300,000 house, they pay £4,500 more in tax than in England. The more expensive the house, the worse that gets. Secondly, Wales has now got a punishing tax for those who buy more expensive homes. For example, a £1 million home in Wales requires £62,000-worth of tax— about half as much again as in England. Now, some people might think that's good. But let me remind you all that Wales has a worryingly small tax base: 1.1 per cent of taxpayers in Wales pay additional tax, compared to 1.5 per cent in the west midlands and 1.9 per cent in the south-west. We should be worried about that. Minister, Wales is getting poorer and the decisions made in this place over 27 years, which you've just reminded us of, have contributed to that. This tax policy was introduced by Mr Mark Drakeford. It acts as an incentive for young people to buy houses in England, and it acts as a disincentive for those who are more wealthy to move to Wales. Your Government claims to want a transformation of the Welsh economy—

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Can we have a question?

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Will you consider changing this structure or, even better, set a target for its abolition?

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: The important piece of this jigsaw that you didn't mention there was that the land transaction tax in Wales has a much higher starting threshold than in England. So, the starting threshold in Wales is £225,000. There are around 55 per cent and more of transactions below the £225,000 threshold in Wales, and they pay no land tax at all—55 per cent of all transactions pay no land transaction tax on a primary residence. The starting threshold in England is £125,000. Every house that is worth more than £125,000, and between £125,000 and £225,000, pays land transaction tax or stamp duty in England. They don't in Wales. In Scotland, it's £145,000. So, in telling the story of land transaction tax, tell it all and then the full picture provides the balanced approach that this Government believes can continue. Although, I am willing to consider whether there is a need to think about first-time buyer relief.  It's something that I'm interested, possibly, in looking at in this context, but very much the majority of first-time buyers are in that context of being under the threshold of £225,000. In fact, that £225,000 threshold is higher than the average house price in Wales of £215,000.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Cabinet Minister, I welcome this Government's commitment to review the land transaction tax and a wider ambition to encourage empty buildings back into use. With Wales barely building half the homes it needs, every empty house counts. One of my constituents in Caerdydd Ffynnon Taf, a small local property developer, has highlighted to me how the tax rules treat uninhabitable properties as residential because they can, in theory, be repaired. But these tumbledown houses, with no services, broken roofs and creeping damp are exactly the ones that we need to become homes. Yet developers pay higher rate land transaction tax on them, discouraging investment and regeneration. Although the empty homes grant helps individual home owners, developers can't use it, and the higher rates refund available for landlords leasing back to councils also doesn't apply. So, as you examine reform, would the Cabinet Minister consider a time-limited tax refund for local developers turning derelict properties into homes? Diolch.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Thank you for that point. As you know, the Government is interested in being able to bring more empty properties back into active use, especially into residential use. And on the point that you made there about the difficulties that some property developers may be finding in renovating and bringing vacant residential properties back into use because they are caught in the land transaction tax matter, and whether there is a way of providing land transaction relief or refund to incentivise property developers bringing properties back, it's an interesting area that I'm perfectly willing to look at as we look at how we use the land transaction tax to enable bringing empty properties back. I certainly wouldn't want it to be an active disincentive, so I will certainly look at how we can see whether there are ways of doing it in a way that enables bringing empty properties back into use.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: 4. What discussions has the Cabinet Minister had with the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language regarding funding for further education? OQ64677
documents.text_cy: 4. Pa drafodaethau y mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet wedi'u cael â'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg ynglŷn â chyllid ar gyfer addysg bellach? OQ64677

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: As part of the budget process, I have regular discussions with all Cabinet Ministers. Decisions on further education funding, like all budget decisions, are considered within wider Cabinet discussions on priorities.
documents.text_cy: Fel rhan o broses y gyllideb, dwi’n cynnal trafodaethau rheolaidd â holl Weinidogion y Cabinet. Mae penderfyniadau ar gyllid addysg bellach, fel pob penderfyniad cyllidebol, yn cael eu hystyried yn ystod trafodaethau ehangach y Cabinet ar flaenoriaethau.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text:
Thank you, Minister. Supporting learners with additional learning needs in the further education sector is becoming a major challenge, with Coleg y Cymoedd telling me that they have experienced almost a 50 per cent increase in the number of learners with ALN and individual development plans during the last academic year. Similarly, the College Merthyr Tydfil identifies not only increasing numbers of students with IDPs, but a stark growth in the numbers of learners identified with an ALN presently undergoing assessment processes to determine whether they require an IDP or additional support arrangements. 

Now, I wholeheartedly welcome the supplementary budget deal that Welsh Labour has secured with your Government, with £60 million extra for additional learning needs, including £2.5 million for further education. But to support learners and staff effectively, this funding needs to be sustainable and long term. So, what discussions will you have with colleagues to ensure that this is the case?

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: I certainly recognise that additional learning needs is a challenge in terms of funding and provision for colleges, post-16 education, as well as our schools. A lot of the focus of the discussion seems to be on schools, but it is a very real challenge for post-16 education as well. That's why I am pleased that, as part of that deal to secure progress on the supplementary budget, and the £60 million allocation for additional learning needs, £2.5 million of that is to go directly to colleges. But another important aspect of that agreement of the £60 million package is that there is an allocation of funding also for the planning for a long-term sustainable model of funding for education and additional needs, so that, over time, we can get to a place where our local authorities, schools and colleges can plan provision to meet the need and the ability to provide education comprehensively for all. We need to get to a better place than we are currently, and that's why we're committed to working with partners across this Chamber on how we can develop and place this on a sustainable footing into the future.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Question 5 [OQ64693] has been withdrawn. Question 6, Sarah Rees.
documents.text_cy: Mae cwestiwn 5 [OQ64693] wedi'i dynnu nôl. Cwestiwn 6, Sarah Rees.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: 6. How will the Cabinet Minister ensure that gender budgeting becomes an integral part of budget development, decision making and scrutiny during this Senedd? OQ64710
documents.text_cy: 6. Sut fydd y Gweinidog Cabinet yn sicrhau bod cyllidebu rhywedd yn dod yn rhan annatod o ddatblygu, gwneud penderfyniadau a chraffu ar y gyllideb yn ystod y Senedd hon? OQ64710

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: This Government is committed to tackling gender inequality and ensuring that equality is properly considered at every stage of budget decision making. Our primary focus as a Government is on the outcomes we achieve, and we must carefully consider which tools and mechanisms help us to make a real difference in people’s lives.
documents.text_cy: Mae’r Llywodraeth hon wedi ymrwymo i fynd i’r afael ag anghydraddoldeb o ran rhywedd a sicrhau bod cydraddoldeb yn cael ei ystyried yn drylwyr ym mhob cam o’r broses o wneud penderfyniadau ar y gyllideb. Ein prif ffocws fel Llywodraeth yw'r canlyniadau rŷn ni’n eu cyflawni, a rhaid inni ystyried yn ofalus ba adnoddau a mecanweithiau sy’n ein helpu ni i wneud gwahaniaeth go iawn i fywydau pobl.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Diolch. I welcome that this Government is working towards its manifesto commitment to embed gender budgeting in Wales. International best practice places that responsibility for this with the Treasury—in that case, you, Minister—because budget decisions shape people's everyday lives. Gender budgeting can seem complex, so I'll attempt an everyday analogy: a good cook does not wait until the guests have eaten to find out whether their recipe worked. Tasting, or testing, happens beforehand, and Government should be no different. Gender budgeting is about assessing the impact of spending decisions before they are made, rather than discovering too late that they've deepened existing inequalities. The case in Wales is stark. Women are three times more likely than men to work part time, three and a half times more likely to be economically inactive, because of caring responsibilities, and face a gender pay gap of 11.8 per cent. So, Minister, what leadership will you show to embed gender budgeting across Government?

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text:
I'm not sure if I'd pass the cook test, but I'll try and pass the budget test. There's a range of tools and approaches that can help us understand the impacts of spending decisions before we take them, and gender budgeting is certainly one of those tools. But there are constraints in terms of our capacity to embed this approach, especially in the context of this year's first budget.

The previous Government undertook gender budgeting pilots that you'll know about, I'm sure, and they provided useful learning. In particular, they highlighted the importance of considering gender early in policy development, rather than adding it later. So, I want to take that learning and consider where it can help us to make better decisions and deliver better outcomes. And if we think of that particularly in the context of where we are developing new programmes—we've spoken of Cynnal, free school swimming and our childcare offer—so that we are using gender budgeting in the context of new policy initiatives, as was highlighted by the gender budgeting pilots—. And, obviously, you've done previous work on gender budgeting, and I'd be happy to discuss this further with you in detail in how we move to embed that across Government as we move through our budgeting processes.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: 7. How will the Welsh Government's tax policies support people in Carmarthenshire? OQ64685 [R]
documents.text_cy: 7. Sut y bydd polisïau treth Llywodraeth Cymru yn cefnogi pobl yn Sir Gaerfyrddin? OQ64685 [R]

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Taxes fund public services that benefit everyone. Fair and proportionate tax policies will support people and businesses in Carmarthenshire. Our changes to rebalance non-domestic rates will benefit communities by supporting vibrant high streets and town centres. The council tax reduction scheme directly supports over 15,000 households in Carmarthenshire.
documents.text_cy: Mae trethi yn ariannu gwasanaethau cyhoeddus sydd o fudd i bawb. Bydd polisïau treth teg a chymesur yn cefnogi pobl a busnesau yn sir Gaerfyrddin. Bydd ein newidiadau i ailgydbwyso trethi busnes o fudd i gymunedau drwy gefnogi'r stryd fawr a chanol trefi ffyniannus. Mae cynllun gostyngiadau'r dreth gyngor yn cefnogi dros 15,000 o aelwydydd yn sir Gaerfyrddin yn uniongyrchol.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Thank you, Cabinet Minister. For many households in Carmarthenshire, the tax that bites the hardest is council tax. Recent analysis found that Welsh councils face a combined projected budget shortfall of more than £272 million next year, with Carmarthenshire's £34 million gap the second highest in Wales. Now, residents are already paying the price. Since 2022, the Plaid Cymru-led county council's band D charge, the benchmark that is used to compare council tax across Wales, and for which every other band is set, has risen by more than 31 per cent, including an 8.9 per cent increase in 2025-26. Council tax may be set locally, but Welsh Ministers already retain powers to intervene where increases are considered excessive. Reform has proposed requiring a local referendum before councils can increase council tax by more than 4.99 per cent, similar to the effective threshold applied to many councils in England. So, will the Welsh Government adopt that protection, so Carmarthenshire residents have the final say before they're hit yet again with rises on the scale that we have seen over the last four years? Diolch.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text:
This is a spoiler alert, but we will be voting against your motion later on. We don't agree that capping local authorities' council tax is a way of enabling local authorities to take the decisions they need to take locally as elected members. The main determinant of council tax is probably still the financial settlement that this Government and this Senedd will pass in February of next year to local authorities. So, us deciding across the Senedd what the scope of that settlement for local authorities will be will be part of the work that we undertake over the next few months.

I already know, and I'm already planning at this point, that our settlement as a Welsh Government will be 0.7 per cent down in real terms for next year. It is a very challenging settlement, unless there are changes from the UK Chancellor at the end of October in his budget. So, that is the crucial determinant of council tax: what is the size of the public sector funding available to local authorities.

I'm hoping, hearing what you say, that you want to see good local settlements for local authorities, and that you will work constructively with us to enable that to happen, just as Plaid Cymru enabled a good settlement to pass by working with the previous Welsh Government so that local government and the NHS were provided the best possible settlement as part of the budget deal of the last Senedd.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: The final question to you, Minister, is question 8. Anthony Slaughter.
documents.text_cy: Y cwestiwn olaf i chi, Weinidog, yw cwestiwn 8. Anthony Slaughter.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: 8. How will the Welsh Government's draft budget for 2027-28 ensure adequate investment in climate resilience? OQ64696
documents.text_cy: 8. Sut y bydd cyllideb ddrafft Llywodraeth Cymru ar gyfer 2027-28 yn sicrhau buddsoddiad digonol o ran gwydnwch hinsawdd? OQ64696

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Climate resilience is an important element of this Government’s work to protect communities and improve outcomes. The draft budget for 2027-28 will support programme for government priorities on climate and nature, including Net Zero Wales, alongside wider Government measures to help Wales adapt to a changing climate.
documents.text_cy: Mae gwydnwch rhag newid hinsawdd yn elfen bwysig o waith y Llywodraeth yma i amddiffyn cymunedau a gwella canlyniadau. Mi fydd y gyllideb ddrafft ar gyfer 2027-28 yn cefnogi blaenoriaethau’r rhaglen lywodraethu sydd yn ymwneud â'r hinsawdd a natur. Mae hyn yn cynnwys Cymru Sero Net, ochr yn ochr â mesurau ehangach y Llywodraeth i helpu Cymru i addasu i hinsawdd sy'n newid.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text:
Diolch. I'm calling on the Welsh Government to create a new extreme weather resilience fund to invest in nature-based interventions to help mitigate the risks from extreme weather. Floods, droughts and wildfires are increasingly prevalent due to climate change, and nature-based solutions are some of the best available defences to protect our communities. If the climate emergency is a genuinely cross-government priority, funding needs to sit in every departmental budget to ensure that no area slips through the cracks.

Evidence from WWF Cymru and others suggests that for relatively small amounts of money within each portfolio, we could see significant cross-cutting benefits, provided that all Welsh Ministers are prepared to show leadership. Can the Minister confirm the amount of money in this year's budget for climate resilience, and will you commit to reviewing existing departmental budgets to find opportunities for nature-based solutions to be ready for the next extreme weather event? Diolch.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text:
Your question highlights probably the very real concerns that we all as elected Members in the Senedd have as to how we face the extreme weather challenges that will face us this winter, as have faced us in the summer past. You know that this Government takes its response and its planning for future events of this nature seriously. The First Minister has convened a summit on climate resilience to happen next week, I think, to bring stakeholders together to continue the discussion on how we prepare and make ourselves more resilient for extreme weather scenarios, because happen they will.

On the issue around how we budget for that, in my initial answer I told you of how we are looking to embed climate change mitigation measures across our budget. You've asked for a specific identification of an extreme weather resilience fund, if I've understood you correctly, across and in each budget allocation and portfolio. That is something that I will certainly think further on and discuss with you and with others in this Chamber. These are ever-changing but very present issues that we need to address as a Government, but also as a Senedd, in how we plan our budgets into the future and how we plan our work.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
documents.text: Thank you very much, Minister.
documents.text_cy: Diolch yn fawr iawn i chi, Weinidog.
