documents.text_cy: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r mater hwn. Rwy'n gwerthfawrogi y bydd hyn yn creu aflonyddwch o ran y gwasanaeth dros dro i deithwyr tra bydd y rheilffordd ar gau. Mae'r Dirprwy Weinidog dros Drafnidiaeth eisoes wedi cyhoeddi datganiad ysgrifenedig. Os oes yna unrhyw bryderon ychwanegol, mi fyddwn i'n eich annog chi i ysgrifennu at yr Aelod. Mae o yma, wrth gwrs, ac wedi clywed yr hyn rydych chi wedi'i godi. Ond, i'ch sicrhau chi, mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ymgysylltu gyda Network Rail ac Avanti a Trafnidiaeth Cymru trwy gyfarfodydd rhwydwaith gogledd Cymru, ac mae Trafnidiaeth Cymru ac Avanti yn cwblhau cynlluniau manwl ar gyfer gwasanaethau bysiau yn lle trenau yn ystod y cyfnod cau hefyd.

documents.item: 2. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Business Manager, can I ask for a joint statement from the Deputy Minister for social care, the Minister for local government and the Minister for education on the pupil development grant for children looked after? The issue I raise is complicated and cuts across multiple portfolios. A recent Estyn report highlighted concerns about the current PDG-CLA funding arrangements. Corporate parenting responsibility remains with the placing authority, but the receiving authorities are required to provide support from their own PDG-CLA allocation. Estyn also reported existing arrangements did not always operate effectively, including inconsistent information sharing and joint working, particularly when learners move between settings, services and local authorities. So, can I have a statement on how the Welsh Government intends to address these issues highlighted in Estyn's report? Diolch.

documents.item: 2. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: I thank the Member for that question. In terms of a statement, it's not the norm to have a joint statement in that way. We do work across Government, of course, and certainly, if you were to write to the Ministers with specific questions, then you would receive that response. But, clearly, the Cabinet Minister for education leads on the pupil development grant, but there is close collaboration between Ministers where there is that overlap. What is important is that we do have that co-operation, because what we're trying to do is to always respond to Estyn recommendations. There is work, of course, for the relevant scrutiny committees in this Senedd and the cross-party group to be looking at such issues, to ensure that implementation is as it should be and that recommendations made by Estyn are progressed.
documents.text_cy: Diolch i'r Aelod am y cwestiwn hwnnw. O ran y datganiad, dydy o ddim yn arferol i gael datganiad ar y cyd yn y modd hwnnw. Mi ydyn ni'n gweithio'n drawslywodraethol ac, yn sicr, pe byddech chi'n ysgrifennu at y Gweinidogion efo'ch cwestiynau penodol, mi fyddech chi'n cael yr ymateb hwnnw. Ond, yn amlwg, y Gweinidog Cabinet dros addysg sy'n arwain o ran y pupil development grant, ond mae cydweithio agos rhwng Gweinidogion lle mae gorgyffwrdd. Yr hyn sy'n bwysig ydy ein bod ni'n cael y cydweithio hwnnw ac mai'r hyn rydyn ni'n ceisio ei gyflawni ydy ymateb bob tro i argymhellion Estyn. Mae yna waith, wrth gwrs, i'r pwyllgorau craffu priodol yn y Senedd hon a grŵp trawsbleidiol i fod yn edrych ar faterion o'r fath, a sicrhau bod y gweithrediad fel y dylai fod a bod argymhellion sy'n cael eu gwneud gan Estyn yn mynd rhagddynt.

documents.item: 2. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Prynhawn da, Drefnydd. I want a statement, please, on the services for women, in particular in rural areas, when they face domestic violence. Last week, two cases in Wales were in our media. In Carmarthen, James McKenna was jailed for 24 years for the attempted murder of his ex-partner, whom he stalked and stabbed repeatedly as she walked her dog. And secondly, there's the really tragic case in Prestatyn, of mother of four Samantha Phythian, who was pregnant and found dead in a burning van. All of these cases, along with the cases of women who are living in rural areas that I represent, show how hard it is for those women to get the services and the responses they need. Could you please give us an update and a statement, and perhaps from the Minister as well, on services for women who face domestic violence and what you're doing to develop these and ensure that they reach everybody? Diolch yn fawr iawn.

documents.item: 2. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: I thank the Member for raising this issue, which received a lot of attention in the press last week, and I would like to say how brave those people who are speaking out about these things are, and it is terrible to hear about that suffering. The Deputy First Minister is here and will have heard what you've raised, and I would like to give you that assurance that we do acknowledge this, that the recent review of the national VAWDASV strategy has noted rural inequality as a key theme in terms of this work. Now, as the new national strategy is developed, I hope that the fact that we have identified this as something that is needed and deserves further attention—. As that review work continues, along with the feedback received, you will have an opportunity, as will others, to scrutinise the Deputy First Minister in relation to that work and to input as well.
documents.text_cy: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi mater, yn amlwg, a gafodd gryn sylw yn y wasg yr wythnos diwethaf, a byddwn i'n hoffi dweud pa mor ddewr ydy pobl sydd yn siarad allan am hyn, ac mae'n erchyll clywed am y dioddefaint hwnnw. Mae'r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog yma ac wedi clywed yr hyn rydych chi wedi ei godi, ond mi fyddwn ni'n hoffi rhoi'r sicrwydd hwnna i chi ein bod ni'n cydnabod hyn, bod yr adolygiad diweddar o'r strategaeth genedlaethol o ran VAWDASV wedi nodi anghydraddoldeb gwledig fel thema allweddol o ran y gwaith hwn. Rŵan, wrth i'r strategaeth genedlaethol newydd gael ei datblygu, dwi'n gobeithio bod y ffaith ein bod ni wedi adnabod hwn fel rhywbeth sydd ei angen ac sy'n haeddu sylw pellach—. Ac wrth gwrs, wrth i'r gwaith adolygu yna fynd rhagddo, gyda'r adborth rydyn ni wedi ei dderbyn, mi fydd yna gyfle i chi ac eraill graffu ar y Dirprwy Brif Weinidog o ran y gwaith hwnnw ac i fewnbynnu.

documents.item: 2. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Trefnydd, I would like a statement from the Government regarding the threat to our most valuable industry, tourism. In Carmarthenshire, tourism earned, in 2024-25, £724 million, employing over 6,600 full-time employees. This is vital to Wales's economy, and we need to listen to the challenge it is facing. I believe this Government doesn't appear to be listening. A whole raft of taxation and regulation is having a serious impact on these businesses. Let's talk about the visitor levy, a tourist tax that is placing another burden on the industry. We are now faced with plans to turn Wales into a giant energy park, with hundreds of enormous wind turbines and pylons in our most beautiful countryside that attracts millions of visitors. Are you aware of the impact? Are you listening to the tourism industry? And what action are you taking to protect it? Diolch.

documents.item: 2. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Well, tourism is hugely important for the Welsh economy, and the Member, I'm sure, will be aware that there are a number of challenges that have been faced by that sector, including the cost-of-living crisis. People have less money in their pockets. There is also the impact of Brexit, which has had an impact on the number of visitors to Wales and to our communities. You're referring to an area that is not implementing the tourism levy at the moment and referring to that as a barrier, and I don't really understand that. We have to look at the facts as they are. Every area will have its own challenges. We also know that there are opportunities that come with some of the things that are in train. But what we are committed to is ensuring that we work with Visit Wales to sell Wales to the world, that we want to ensure that tourism can prosper and that we support those businesses. It is central as regards what was in our manifesto and to the work that we are looking at on a cross-ministerial basis. As a Government, I, as Minister with responsibility for culture and sport, also believe that we're not taking full advantage of the tourism related to our history, our culture, and the opportunities that comes with major events such as the Tour de France and the Euros in 2028. Therefore, tourism is hugely important to this Government and we are working on a cross-ministerial basis on it.

Mae gan bobl lai o arian yn eu pocedi. Mae Brexit hefyd, er enghraifft, wedi cael effaith ar nifer y bobl sy'n dod i Gymru a'n cymunedau ni. Rydych chi'n cyfeirio at ardal sydd ddim yn mynd rhagddo efo'r lefi twristiaeth ar y funud, gan nodi hwnna fel rhwystr, a dwi ddim yn deall hynny. Mae'n rhaid i ni edrych ar y ffeithiau. Mi fydd pob ardal efo'i heriau gwahanol. Rydyn ni hefyd yn gwybod bod yna gyfleon yn dod efo rhai o'r pethau sydd mewn grym. Ond yr hyn rydyn ni wedi ymrwymo iddo fo ydy sicrhau ein bod ni'n gweithio gyda Chroeso Cymru i werthu Cymru i'r byd, ein bod ni eisiau sicrhau bod twristiaeth yn gallu ffynnu a'n bod ni'n cefnogi'r busnesau hynny. Mae o'n ganolog o ran yr hyn rydyn ni wedi ei roi yn ein maniffesto ni a'r gwaith rydyn ni'n edrych yn drawsweinidigol arno fo. documents.item: 2. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Trefnydd, I'd like to request a statement on transport accessibility for blind and partially sighted people from the Deputy Minister for Transport to understand what more can be done to ensure everyone can travel safely, confidently and independently. Last week, I had the privilege of spending the morning with Rachel from the Royal National Institute of Blind People and her guide dog, Flick, as we attempted to walk from the bus station in Wrexham to the train station. I was provided a pair of goggles to help me understand Rachel's visual impairment. What struck me was the daily challenges facing people with sight loss in navigating their surroundings and accessing public transport. Access to public transport is essential for people to maintain their independence, access healthcare and stay connected to their communities. It's important that buses, trains and transport infrastructure are accessible, and that people with sight loss feel safe when travelling, certainly to avoid any risk of isolation. So, I'd be grateful for a statement from the Deputy Minister to highlight the work undertaken by the Welsh Government to ensure that blind and partially sighted people can access this transport as easily as possible. Thank you.

Certainly, the Deputy Minister for Transport is present and has heard what you've raised, and he has expressed to me that he's willing to bring an update to Members through a written statement.

documents.item: 2. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Trefnydd, I would like to request an urgent Government statement on the independence, accountability and powers of Care Inspectorate Wales. When social services fail, accountability cannot be optional. Section 150 of Social Services and Well-being (Wales) Act 2014 sets out clear statutory grounds for intervention where a local authority fails, or is likely to fail, in the exercise of its social services functions. Section 152 then gives Welsh Ministers the power to intervene where statutory conditions aren't met. Yet, Care Inspectorate Wales exercises its functions on behalf of Welsh Ministers. That raises a serious question about whether professional independence goes far enough. Families affected by serious failures deserve a regulator whose structural independence is beyond question, with powers necessary to expose systematic problems and ensure they are acted upon. Will the Government, therefore, bring forward an urgent statement setting out precisely how it will ensure that Care Inspectorate Wales can make decisions independently of Welsh Ministers, while remaining fully transparent and accountable to the people of Wales and the Senedd? Diolch.

documents.item: 2. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Business Minister, can I please request an urgent statement from the Welsh Government about the proposed closure of the three junctions alongside the M4 in Newport? All residents know that shutting down junctions 27, 26 and 25 on the M4 would be disastrous and cause nothing but chaos and mayhem across the city, with traffic being pushed into already congested routes. Now, news of the Government's junction closure plans has sparked anger and uproar in Newport, with constituents inundating me and other MSs with e-mails, calls and also letters. The message is clear: they want the Government to keep their hands off our motorway junctions. And I've spoken to numerous constituents living near junction 27 who've told me that they're seriously considering moving and selling up because they just can't handle what's going to be coming their way. And it's not just residents and businesses who have serious concerns over the Government plans. Gwent police and crime commissioner has warned that these closures could pose a serious risk to our emergency service response times, going forward. The Government has insisted that it will listen to the concerns and voice of those directly impacted by these plans, but we haven't heard how exactly this is going to be achieved. So, an urgent statement from the Government outlining its plans, how it's going to be consulting with residents, businesses and emergency services, as well as others, and when this work will start, is urgently needed by us all. Thank you.

documents.item: 2. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text:
I hope that the Member heard the oral statement last week. I don't think there has been a lack of opportunity to scrutinise and to ask the Minister questions. So, I don't think that a statement so soon after that is appropriate, in particular because, let's bear in mind, of what was noted, which was that we're now going to be looking at considering the evidence, understanding the different facts and options, and working towards solutions that improve journeys whilst supporting communities, businesses and the broader economy. So, as to all of the concerns that you have set out, that's exactly what will be happening now: listening.

I'm sure as well that the Member—like all Members here, I hope—wants to see this Government taking action. We have seen 27 years of a lack of action and a lack of solutions, so we have to move forward with this work. The engagement work is happening at the moment, and everyone with concerns has an opportunity to be part of this. It was announced last week that there would be more updates and opportunities for people to be engaging. So, I hope that we will be able to unite behind the fact that the Minister has outlined a way forward finally, and there will be an opportunity for those who have concerns to express those. But we do have to see a solution. I'm sure the Member agrees with me on that.

documents.item: 2. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Good afternoon, Trefnydd. Since questioning the First Minister on NHS dental care last week, I have had countless constituents and people across Wales get in contact. One said that they have waited unsuccessfully since 2019 to get back on an NHS list, now facing £800-plus for root canal treatment. Another says they finally secured NHS care, only to be restricted to emergency treatment due to the new dental contract. Another says their practice has gone private, demanding £264 a year just for membership fees. This is the reality of your fundamentally flawed dental contract. A new dental school is welcome, of course it is, but it is the contract that needs reworking, and this Government needs to listen, as I said last week, to practising dentists to make the contract fit for purpose. A lack of NHS dental care is now a national emergency, and I believe this requires an urgent statement on the floor of this Senedd or a debate to address this. Diolch.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text:
Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Today, I am updating Members on the next steps regarding the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order submitted to Welsh Ministers by Natural Resources Wales in January of this year.

Following careful consideration of the designation Order, the evidence assembled by Natural Resources Wales, the representations and objections received during the designation process, and the associated impact assessments, I have reached a provisional view in respect of the question of whether to confirm, confirm with modifications or to reject the designation Order. I am currently minded not to confirm the designation Order, and consequently minded not to proceed with a public local inquiry at this stage. Not confirming the designation Order and not proceeding with a public local inquiry will mean that no new national park is established at this time.

I do want to be clear with Members that this is not a final decision. Before reaching a final decision, I intend to provide a short opportunity for everyone with an interest in this proposal to make further representations in respect of the provisional view that I have reached.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text:
Members will be aware that the previous administration asked Natural Resources Wales to assess the case for a new national park. Following an extensive programme of evidence gathering, engagement and consultation, NRW concluded that the area comprising the proposed Glyndŵr national park did meet the statutory tests for designation, and submitted the designation Order to Welsh Ministers.

Since then, a significant volume of evidence has been gathered. Over 400 responses were received during the notification period. These reflected a variety of views, with many respondents supporting the proposal and many opposing it. Significant objections were also submitted, including objections from every one of the five local authorities in the area. There were strong feelings in favour and strong feelings against. Many have highlighted the potential benefits: these include opportunities to enhance nature recovery, strengthen climate resilience, provide strategic leadership for landscape management, and support recreation and sustainable tourism. The evidence presented by NRW identifies a number of opportunities in these areas.

At the same time, important questions have been raised throughout the process relating to affordability, funding requirements in the future, value for money, governance arrangements and potential impacts on local communities, infrastructure, energy developments, housing and the Welsh language. These concerns have been raised by local authorities, businesses and land managers.

In reaching my provisional view, I have carefully considered these issues. I have considered the findings of the regulatory impact assessment and integrated impact assessment prepared by officials. That analysis highlights both possible benefits and significant uncertainties. The regulatory impact assessment estimates establishment costs of over £11 million and identifies ongoing costs associated with establishing and operating a new national park authority. It also notes uncertainty in the evidence base.

Roedd y rhain yn adlewyrchu amrywiaeth o safbwyntiau, gyda llawer o ymatebwyr yn cefnogi a llawer yn gwrthwynebu. Cyflwynwyd gwrthwynebiadau sylweddol hefyd, gan gynnwys gwrthwynebiadau gan bob un o'r pum awdurdod lleol yn yr ardal berthnasol. Teimladau cryf o blaid a theimladau cryf yn erbyn. Mae llawer wedi tynnu sylw at y manteision posibl: cyfleoedd i adfer natur, gwrthsefyll newid hinsawdd yn well, rhoi arweiniad strategol ar gyfer rheoli'r dirwedd, cefnogi hamddena a thwristiaeth gynaliadwy. documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text:
As I have already noted, all five local authorities in the area objected to the designation. While I have carefully considered all representations received, I do recognise the importance of understanding the views of these local authorities, which already play a role in delivering many of the outcomes that are sought through designation and which would be important partners should a national park ultimately be established.

I therefore consider that there is great value in continuing to maintain a strong focus on enabling those existing designations and partnerships to deliver for nature, climate, cultural heritage, recreation and local communities, while continuing to pursue the objectives identified through the Glyndŵr park designation process through other mechanisms. For example, we are taking practical action to restore nature and build climate resilience across the north-east. Through the Welsh Government’s national peatland programme, significant restoration work has been delivered within the Clwydian range and Dee valley national landscape, including at Llandegla moor site, which is of special scientific interest, bringing around 120 hectares of peatland into a more favourable condition.

The evidence demonstrates that many of the challenges identified by Natural Resources Wales are already being addressed through this Welsh Government's current programmes. These include our work on biodiversity recovery, peatland restoration, nature networks, the sustainable farming scheme, including Ffermio Bro, climate and nature action, sustainable tourism and wider rural investment.

Importantly, these policies are already delivering real outcomes for communities, farmers and the environment. Ffermio Bro, our bespoke sustainable farming scheme for designated landscapes, is supporting farmers to deliver practical action for nature recovery, climate resilience and sustainable land management. Farmers at Llangwyfan farm are restoring hedgerows to reconnect ancient woodland and improve woodland management to strengthen habitats for native flora and fauna. This is helping to create a more connected and resilient landscape. It therefore appears to me that the objectives identified through the designation process may be delivered through alternative mechanisms, without establishing a new national park authority and without incurring the ongoing financial commitments that the designation would require.

Looking ahead, I believe there will be further opportunities to secure these outcomes through the Welsh Government's work, through our climate and nature action plan, our culture strategy, our proposed rural-proofing and environmental sustainability duty, which will strengthen the consideration of environmental sustainability, climate resilience and rural impacts across public sector decision making. I will also consider whether existing arrangements for national landscapes can be further strengthened, alongside other integrated approaches that support nature recovery, sustainable land management and thriving rural communities.

Having said all that, I do recognise the significance of this proposal in front of us today and the strong interest it continues to generate. My responsibility is to reach a reasonable conclusion on the basis of all the relevant information. It's for that reason that I am not making a final decision today. Instead, I invite any party to submit further representations before reaching a final decision.

This is therefore an opportunity for local authorities, representative organisations, businesses, community groups and members of the public to present any additional evidence, arguments or material considerations that they believe Welsh Ministers should take into account. People and organisations can submit their views via e-mail or through the post, the details of which will be on the Welsh Government's website as we bring the statement in the Senedd today to a close. I will also be publishing links to a range of evidence that has been developed during the process so far to further inform these considerations. I would encourage people to provide new evidence, in particular, or information that has not already been considered through the extensive work carried out to date.

The intention of these steps is not to repeat earlier consultation exercises; rather, it is intended to ensure that all relevant evidence has been properly considered and in a reasonable manner before a final decision is made. Once this period has concluded, in four weeks' time, officials will analyse the representations received and provide further advice to me. Then I will consider all submissions carefully before coming to a final decision, as well as publishing my reasons.

The landscapes, communities and cultural heritage of the north-east are nationally important. Whatever the final outcome, the evidence assembled over recent years has highlighted both their special qualities and the challenges they face. I remain committed to working with partners to secure positive outcomes for those landscapes, communities and future generations. Note again that this announcement represents a provisional view only. I encourage all interested parties to engage constructively with the next steps so that any final decision is informed by the fullest possible consideration of the evidence before us. Thank you very much.

Fel dwi eisoes wedi'i nodi, gwnaeth y pum awdurdod lleol yn yr ardal wrthwynebu'r dynodiad. Er fy mod wedi ystyried yn ofalus yr holl sylwadau sydd wedi dod i law, dwi'n cydnabod ei bod yn bwysig iawn deall barn yr awdurdodau lleol yma, sydd eisoes yn chwarae rhan wrth gyflawni llawer o’r canlyniadau a geisir trwy ddynodi ac a fyddai’n bartneriaid pwysig pe bai parc cenedlaethol yn cael ei sefydlu yn y pen draw.

Dwi'n ystyried felly fod gwerth mawr mewn parhau i gadw ffocws cryf ar alluogi'r dynodiadau a'r partneriaethau presennol yma i gyflawni ar gyfer natur, hinsawdd, treftadaeth ddiwylliannol, hamdden a chymunedau lleol, tra'n parhau i fynd ar drywydd yr amcanion a nodwyd drwy broses ddynodi parc Glyndŵr drwy fecanweithiau eraill. Er enghraifft, rŷn ni'n cymryd camau ymarferol i adfer natur ac adeiladu gwydnwch hinsawdd ar draws y gogledd-ddwyrain. Drwy raglen genedlaethol mawndir Llywodraeth Cymru, cyflawnwyd gwaith adfer sylweddol o fewn tirwedd genedlaethol bryniau Clwyd a dyffryn Dyfrdwy, gan gynnwys safle rhostir Llandegla sydd o ddiddordeb gwyddonol arbennig, gan ddod â thua 120 hectar o fawndir i gyflwr gwell.

Mae'r dystiolaeth yn dangos bod llawer o'r heriau a nodwyd gan Gyfoeth Naturiol Cymru eisoes dan ystyriaeth gan raglenni presennol y Llywodraeth hon. Yn eu plith mae ein gwaith ar adfer bioamrywiaeth, adfer mawndiroedd, rhwydweithiau natur, y cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy, gan gynnwys Ffermio Bro, gweithredu ar hinsawdd a natur, twristiaeth gynaliadwy a buddsoddi ehangach yng nghefn gwlad.

Yn bwysig, mae'r polisïau yma eisoes yn cyflawni canlyniadau gwirioneddol i gymunedau, ffermwyr a'r amgylchedd. Mae Ffermio Bro, ein cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy pwrpasol ar gyfer tirweddau dynodedig, yn cefnogi ffermwyr i weithredu’n ymarferol ar gyfer adferiad natur, gwydnwch hinsawdd a rheoli tir cynaliadwy. Mae ffermwyr yn fferm Llangwyfan yn adfer gwrychoedd i ailgysylltu coetir hynafol a gwella rheoli coetiroedd i gryfhau cynefinoedd ar gyfer fflora a ffawna brodorol. Mae hyn yn helpu i greu tirwedd fwy cysylltiedig a gwydn. Mae'n ymddangos i mi, felly, y gellir cyflawni'r amcanion a gafodd eu nodi gan y broses ddynodi trwy fecanweithiau amgen, heb sefydlu awdurdod parc cenedlaethol newydd a heb ysgwyddo'r ymrwymiadau ariannol y byddai ar y dynodiad eu hangen wedi hynny.

Wrth edrych ymlaen, dwi'n credu bydd yna gyfleoedd pellach i sicrhau'r canlyniadau hyn drwy waith y Llywodraeth, drwy ein cynllun gweithredu hinsawdd a natur sydd ar ein gweill, ein strategaeth ddiwylliant, ein dyletswydd diogelu gwledig a chynaliadwyedd amgylcheddol arfaethedig, a fydd yn cryfhau'r ystyriaeth o gynaliadwyedd amgylcheddol, gwydnwch hinsawdd ac effeithiau gwledig ar draws penderfyniadau'r sector cyhoeddus. Dwi hefyd am ystyried a ellir cryfhau'r trefniadau presennol ar gyfer tirweddau cenedlaethol, ochr yn ochr â dulliau integredig eraill sy'n cefnogi adferiad natur, rheoli tir cynaliadwy a chymunedau gwledig ffyniannus.

Wedi dweud hynny i gyd, dwi'n cydnabod arwyddocâd y cynnig hwn sydd o'n blaenau heddiw a'r diddordeb mawr sydd ynddo. Fy nghyfrifoldeb i yw dod i gasgliad rhesymol ar sail yr holl wybodaeth berthnasol. Am y rheswm hwnnw, dwi ddim am wneud penderfyniad terfynol heddiw. Yn hytrach, dwi’n gwahodd unrhyw barti i gyflwyno sylwadau pellach cyn inni wneud penderfyniad terfynol.

Dyma gyfle felly i awdurdodau lleol, sefydliadau cynrychioladol, busnesau, grwpiau cymunedol ac aelodau o'r cyhoedd gyflwyno unrhyw dystiolaeth, dadleuon neu ystyriaethau materol ychwanegol y credant y dylai Gweinidogion Cymru eu hystyried. Gall pobl a sefydliadau gyflwyno'u barn drwy e-bost neu drwy'r post, a bydd y manylion ar wefan Llywodraeth Cymru wrth i ni ddod i ddiwedd y datganiad hwn yn y Senedd heddiw. Byddaf hefyd yn cyhoeddi dolenni i ystod o'r dystiolaeth sydd wedi'i ddatblygu yn ystod y broses hyd yma i lywio'r ystyriaethau ymhellach. Byddwn i'n annog pobl i gyflwyno sylwadau yn benodol sy'n darparu tystiolaeth neu wybodaeth newydd nad ydynt eisoes wedi eu hystyried drwy'r gwaith helaeth a wnaed hyd yn hyn.

Nid bwriad y camau hyn yw ailadrodd ymarferion ymgynghori cynharach; yn hytrach, mae'n bwriadu sicrhau bod yr holl dystiolaeth berthnasol wedi ei hystyried yn briodol ac yn rhesymol cyn gwneud penderfyniad terfynol. Ar ôl i'r cyfnod hwn ddod i ben, mewn pedair wythnos, bydd swyddogion yn dadansoddi'r sylwadau a dderbyniwyd ac yn rhoi cyngor pellach i mi. Yna byddaf yn ystyried yr holl gyflwyniadau yn ofalus cyn dod i benderfyniad terfynol, ynghyd â chyhoeddi fy rhesymau.

Mae tirweddau cymunedau a threftadaeth ddiwylliannol y gogledd-ddwyrain yn bwysig yn genedlaethol. Beth bynnag yw'r canlyniad terfynol, mae'r dystiolaeth a gasglwyd dros y blynyddoedd diwethaf wedi tynnu sylw at eu rhinweddau arbennig a'r heriau maen nhw'n eu hwynebu. Dwi'n parhau i ymrwymo i weithio gyda phartneriaid i sicrhau canlyniadau cadarnhaol i'r tirweddau, i'r cymunedau a chenedlaethau'r dyfodol. Nodwch eto: mae'r cyhoeddiad hwn yn cynrychioli barn dros dro yn unig. Dwi'n annog pawb sydd â diddordeb i ymgysylltu'n adeiladol ar y camau nesaf, fel bod unrhyw benderfyniad terfynol yn cael ei lywio gan yr ystyriaeth lawnaf bosib o'r dystiolaeth sydd o'n blaenau. Diolch yn fawr.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text: Thank you very much, Minister. Adrian Mason.
documents.text_cy: Diolch yn fawr iawn, Weinidog. Adrian Mason.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text:
Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Cabinet Minister, we've only known each other for a few months, but during that time I've found you to be a reasonable man, and quite frankly, we have political differences, but I know that, as I do, you have the best interests of the people of Wales. So, as such, your statement on a proposed new national park for Wales is welcome. In this instance, nobody in this Chamber needs convincing that the Clwydian range, the Dee valley and the wider area covered by the proposal contain some of the finest landscapes in Wales; they're absolutely fantastic. However, that is not the issue; the issue is determining whether a new national park with associated new powers and costs is the right answer. 

Cabinet Minister, I applaud your recognition that there remain too many unanswered questions to confirm the designation Order or to conduct a public inquiry at the moment. We know that Natural Resources Wales believes the area meets the statutory test for designation. However, we also know that serious concerns remain. Numerous opposition points have been raised by stakeholders. Denbighshire has maintained its objection. Flintshire has raised concerns surrounding costs, duplication of planning, amongst others. These concerns matter because this isn't simply about drawing a line on a map, is it? People live within these lines. They farm, they run businesses, they raise families, and basically they're entitled to know what this proposal will actually mean for their lives and livelihoods. That's paramount. They deserve absolute transparency.

So, Cabinet Minister, I appreciate your commitment to pausing proposals in light of the continued uncertainty. Your recognition of the affordability question and what makes commercial common sense for Wales is welcome. These proposals intersect with Wales's best financial interests and the heart of Welsh communities. The important question now is what will happen afterwards or to these proposals.

You've made it clear that your statement today is not a final decision, and have committed to giving an opportunity to those with an interest in these proposals to make further representations. But after the four weeks' extended consultation period, what will happen next? You have committed to ensuring officials will analyse the representations and provide further advice; however, the representations of the interested parties must be listened to—not simply heard, but listened to. Because if local government, communities and other interested parties are to feel confident in the proposals, they must be confident that their views have been listened to and are capable of influencing the final decision.

When looking at the area in question, it's clear that statistics on tourist footfall are positive. In the 2025 statutory consultation report, Natural Resources Wales found that the area already draws 3.3 million visitors annually. Cabinet Minister, it is the right decision not to push forward with the proposals with an incomplete evidence base when it cannot be guaranteed that councils such as Denbighshire, Flintshire, Wrexham and others will not end up carrying additional costs, whether directly or indirectly.

Then there's the effect on local communities, of course. A national park is not simply scenery. There are legitimate concerns about housing development, tourism, traffic and the ability of younger people to remain in the communities where they grew up, with implications for the Welsh language, of course. These concerns should not be dismissed as hostility to environmental protection. They are practical questions about how this proposal will work in the real world.

And finally, Cabinet Minister, there is a question of trust, isn't there? The law provides for objections to be heard for a jolly good reason. Affected county councils and communities have already raised serious issues. Basically, they need to discuss these matters further. I applaud your commitment to exploring how the objectives of the designating process can be delivered under alternative arrangements, and without the £11.6 million estimated establishment cost. We need to understand the fundamentals before prioritising designation: what issues does a new national park solve, why is this particular structure the right solution, how will it work, how will it be funded, and who will be accountable when decisions go wrong.

Cabinet Minister, in light of persistent unanswered questions, the decision not to pursue these proposals before further representations are made across the board is absolutely the right one. Should your Government answer these questions in the affirmative and make a clear financial and local case for proposals, we in Reform will look positively upon the proposals and we will support it, but only if it reflects the wishes of the people of the communities most directly affected. Before another layer of Government is created in north-east Wales, those questions deserve clear answers. The purpose of this Chamber is to represent the interests of the Welsh people—

documents.text: Can I ask you to conclude, please?

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text: Indeed you can. In light of today's statement, Cabinet Minister, I am confident that the correct steps have been taken to ensure Welsh voices have not just been acknowledged but been listened to. Thank you.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text: Thank you to the opposition spokesperson for his comments. My intention, Dirprwy Lywydd, is not to get into immense detail in my responses, because we are now in a phase of listening. I have set out the rationale for why I will be listening over the next four weeks before I make my final decision. But the points are clearly well made by the opposition spokesperson, and I thank him for those comments.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text:
I thank the Cabinet Minister for his statement, but this is a disappointing and, I would add, weak statement from the Minister that demonstrates two things: firstly, a lack of ambition from this Plaid Cymru Government and, secondly, a divide on the Government side when it comes to environmental issues. I think people watching will be surprised to learn that Plaid Cymru, a party that says it wants to tackle the nature emergency, is not progressive when it comes to the environment or on improving access to nature, and surprised that, rather than taking steps to consult the public and get Glyndŵr over the finishing line, the Cabinet Minister has instead chosen to duck his responsibility with what is effectively half a decision.

We are fortunate in Wales that we have beautiful natural environments, and national parks are a great way of opening up our natural environment so more people can enjoy the beautiful places we have in Wales. In Government, Welsh Labour cherished and protected our natural environment and we recognised the huge potential of a new national park. We were ambitious to press ahead. It was a firm manifesto commitment from us. We launched that public inquiry to take the final steps towards establishing Glyndŵr, which would be Wales's first new national park in almost 70 years. The Campaign for National Parks has said that to not go ahead with a public inquiry, as the Cabinet Minister has laid out, would be a bitterly disappointing retreat from this Government, especially from one that has supposedly committed to the protection and restoration of nature-rich landscapes. So, does the Minister agree that this is a retreat?

In your statement, Minister, you said that many respondents supported the proposal and many opposed it. But can you confirm that a majority of respondents were actually in favour of a new national park? Minister, you also said there's now a short opportunity for interested parties to try to change the Government's position. Can you set out the time frame for people to make representations to the Government about this? What advice do you give to those interested about the most effective way of making their case heard? When can we expect you, Minister, to reach a final decision, rather than today's part decision? And why, Minister, do you now think that a 'short opportunity' is preferable to a proper public inquiry, which would have looked in more detail at the evidence and the arguments for and against Glyndŵr? 

Lastly, people will rightly ask why a Government that across every other aspect of public policy is so in favour of reviews and inquiries has decided not to have a public inquiry on this occasion. Can I ask the Minister whether there was any new evidence that prompted his statement today, or was it always the Government's intention to cancel a public inquiry and stop Glyndŵr from progressing? Diolch.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text:
Thank you to the opposition spokesperson for those questions. There are some points of substance there. I've heard the view expressed clearly, which I will obviously take into account, and I will reiterate my request to anyone who has an interest in these matters to write to the Government through the Welsh Government website or through the Royal Mail to offer us their views. I will welcome those views, and I will consider them carefully and reasonably.

It is a period of four weeks, and that is the timetable. It would be my intention, and I have asked my officials, to assess and analyse those representations in short order, because I do not believe that uncertainty helps anyone. I would hope to be in a position to update this Senedd either by Christmas or early in the new year as to the next steps—the next step either being the commissioning of a public inquiry or a rejection of the designation Order.

There is a point raised here about whether we should always turn to a public inquiry or to a 54:46 result on a consultation to guide us as a Government. Fundamentally, it is my belief that Government Ministers must make political judgments. At times, those judgments will be balanced, and there will be people who are proponents of one side or the other, but we have to consider the evidence carefully and come to a conclusion. That is what I have sought to do here, and I have set out a follow-on process that will allow people to make further representations. Diolch.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text:
Well, you have parked the national park. I want to welcome that announcement. It's absolutely necessary, because whilst I support the principle of a national park in north-east Wales, I was not impressed with the proposals that were put forward by Natural Resources Wales, which seem to have gone bonkers with the felt-tip pen, drawing a huge area into the new proposed national park. I did not believe that that represented the opportunity for north-east Wales that it ought to have done. I have always believed that, had a national park been able to be established, it should have been established along the borders of the existing area of outstanding natural beauty in the Clwydian range and the Dee valley. Nor was I supportive of the establishment of a new national park authority, because we all know the democratic deficit that exists in national park authorities, with people who are appointed to them rather than people who are directly accountable to members of the public in those national park areas. That is something that I would hope the Government could reflect on for other national parks in Wales, and whether there may be an opportunity to undertake a piece of work on reform for national parks.

I have to say, I heard the bleating from the Labour Party about this. They had five years to deliver a national park. It was one of the key commitments that they say their party made in advance of the Senedd elections in 2021. We know that they failed to fulfil many of their promises; this was on that long list of promises that they failed to fulfil. And if it was so important to them, perhaps you could have asked for this as part of the budget deal that you've just given to the Plaid Cymru Government. Because you could have extracted a much higher price, frankly, than the peanuts that you seem to have accepted in return for your votes on the supplementary budget when it comes in a few weeks' time.

You've identified the timetable, which is good, because I don't think the uncertainty helps anybody in north Wales, particularly those who were fearful about the implications of a national park. Can you tell me this, though, Minister? You mentioned the cost of the establishment of the national park, the £11.6 million. That money has been provided for, if you like, within the budget, I would assume, over the next few years, has it not? [Interruption.] No. Okay. So, it's not in your thinking, not in your psyche, which seems a bit odd. [Interruption.] The reason I'm asking is because I would still like that investment to flow into the existing AONB, because I do think that protecting our designated landscapes is important. We know that there are issues with the capacity of car parks, the maintenance of footpaths, the need for rangers, if you like, to make sure that our designated landscapes, including AONBs, are properly managed. I do think that there is a need for further resources to be invested in north-east Wales in the Clwydian range and Dee valley AONB. Of course, you would expect me to argue that, as a person who represents that neck of the woods.

But I do urge you, in making your final determination on this: don't shy away from making a brave decision to abandon the project altogether if necessary, because we've got to do what's right for the people in those communities that are affected by this. I heard the comments about impact on the Welsh language, and impact on house prices as well, of course, which has been raised by many people in response to the consultation. But what we've really got to do is make sure that the beauty that we're all able to enjoy in north-east Wales is something that we can continue to offer to people, to visitors, to take advantage of the economic benefits that those visitors can bring to our communities, but in a way that is well managed, in a way that supports appropriate development, that doesn't hinder responsible landowners from continuing to be able to manage their land in a way that protects the environment, and also in a way that is efficient for the taxpayer.

That's why I would urge you, please, to consider looking at the reform of national parks to see whether there's a different way forward, and whether designated landscapes can be managed in a different way—rather than by national park authorities, whether they can be managed by local authorities in those areas, in the same way that the AONB is successfully managed in north Wales. Because I do think that's a more efficient way for the taxpayer to still get the benefits that these designations bring.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text: I thank the Member for those generally positive comments. As my colleague has highlighted, there was no money allocated in the previous Government's budget for this purpose, which I think is interesting, shall we say. You make some interesting points more broadly about the governance of national parks. It is something that I shall certainly be considering and my colleagues will certainly be considering. The landscape of governance in Wales is potentially more complicated than it needs to be. How we move from here to where we would like to be is another question and I'm sure we will have lively debates in this Senedd around some of those issues. But it is a point well made.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text: Thank you, Minister. This is the reality of what a new national park would mean: joining together the area from Llangadfan in Powys to Prestatyn, areas that have nothing whatsoever in common. Increasing house prices 25 per cent above the average, according to Nationwide building society, making the situation even worse for our young people. Increasing transport pressures as a result of the enchanting make-believe image of national parks in areas like Llanrhaeadr-ym-Mochnant and Llanddwyn, while doing nothing to improve biodiversity, according to recent studies, compared to areas outside of the park, while costing approximately £6 million per annum, at a time when existing parks have faced funding cuts of 41 per cent, and are under huge pressure, and while our rural services also face constant cuts. Creating a new authority is neither sustainable nor appropriate, and £2.1 million has already been wasted on this by the previous Government. Enough is enough. Could I have confirmation that this Government will not spend a fortune on the next phase of this process?
documents.text_cy: Diolch, Weinidog. Dyma chi'r realiti y byddai parc cenedlaethol newydd yn ei olygu: uno'r ardal o Langadfan ym Mhowys i Brestatyn ynghyd, sydd â dim byd yn gyffredin â'i gilydd. Cynyddu prisiau tai 25 y cant yn uwch na'r cyfartaledd yn ôl cymdeithas dai y Nationwide, gan wneud pethau hyd yn oed yn waeth i'n pobl ifanc. Cynyddu pwysau trafnidiaeth yn sgil delwedd hud a lledrith statws parc cenedlaethol ar lefydd fel Llanrhaeadr-ym-Mochnant a Llanwddyn, tra'n gwneud dim gwahaniaeth i fioamrywiaeth, yn ôl astudiaethau diweddar, o gymharu â thu allan i barciau cenedlaethol, tra’n costio tua £6 miliwn y flwyddyn ar adeg pan fo parciau sydd eisoes yn bodoli wedi cael toriadau cyllidol o 41 y cant, ac o dan bwysau dybryd, a thra bod ein gwasanaethau gwledig yn cael eu torri o hyd. Dyw cael awdurdod newydd ddim yn gynaliadwy nac yn briodol, a gwastraffwyd £2.1 miliwn eisoes gan y Llywodraeth flaenorol ar hyn. Digon yw digon. A ellir cael cadarnhad na fydd y Llywodraeth yma yn gwario ffortiwn ar y cam nesaf hyn?

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text: I thank the Member. I can confirm that we won't be spending a fortune, but recommending that people send their comments via e-mail in the next phase. We won't be spending a great amount of money on the analysis either. That is, we need to make a wise decision on these issues as a matter of urgency.
documents.text_cy: Diolch i’r Aelod. Mi allaf i gadarnhau na fyddwn ni'n gwario ffortiwn, ond yn argymell pobl i hala e-bost atom ni gyda’u sylwadau nhw yn y cam nesaf—nag ar y dadansoddi chwaith. Hynny yw, mae angen i ni symud ymlaen i ddod i benderfyniad rhesymol a chall ar y materion yma rhag blaen.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text:
Cabinet Minister, I really do welcome the decision, actually—although it's only provisional so far—not to proceed with yet another publicly funded authority. Now, you've also acknowledged that existing organisations and bodies can already deliver the same objectives that a national park would do if it was to be introduced, and I'll come to that at the end. But, surely, the evidence in front of us now raises a bigger question, and that is: why was this proposal allowed to progress this far in the first place? 

If this does ever proceed, obviously, as was alluded to earlier, it's going to cost £11.6 million just to establish it, plus further ongoing costs, despite objections from every single one of the other affected local authorities. So, I'd like to know, really: how much taxpayers' money has already been spent pursuing this proposal? Also, will you now commit to rejecting it permanently, please, rather than leaving the door open to yet another expensive layer of bureaucracy that local communities neither need nor want?

Now, finally, as I've alluded to just now, you've confirmed that the work of all local authorities can be carried out without them—

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text: Can you conclude, please?

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text: So, I'd just like to sort of echo the comment that was made over there, but go further than that, and that is to confirm that, if we don't need these other national park authorities, we should get rid of them all in the first place. Thank you.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text:
I thank the Member for the question. I think allusion has been made to the sum spent by a previous Government on this programme, and I've given a commitment to the Senedd that, over this next period, we will be spending very little indeed in simply assessing the information we get in, and affording an opportunity for people to e-mail us. 

I understand the point made that it should be rejected permanently today. I am minded towards that point of view, but, for the reasons I've outlined, I have set out that extra short process, so that interested parties—. Because it is not a matter of consensus, even across this Chamber, but I am minded to make that decision. I have set out the reasons why I am minded to make that decision, but I have also set out a short timescale for reaching that decision. 

You raise an interesting point, and maybe I may make some positive points about the previous Government here. The financial context that we face is clearly an issue. I think, if we were in a position, if we were back in the halcyon dates of public sector growth in spending between 1997 and 2005, we might be having a different discussion here. I'm sceptical about layers of bureaucracy generally, but if the financial position was different—. I think that is an issue. 

I also think—and it is something that I'm hoping to bring to my role, and colleagues are hoping to bring to their role—that we have, as a Senedd, and as a Government in past years, sought out major pieces of legislation, major new initiatives, without following through every time on working out what the outcomes will be for people in communities right across Wales. And if we can bring that focus back to outcomes and to making an improvement to people's lives, we can improve housing, the Welsh language, businesses, tourism, sustainability, in a more integrated way. So, I think there is an opportunity there to bring things together across Government.

As I've set out, I am not persuaded that that requires a new national park in the Glyndŵr area, as of today. I've offered that opportunity for people to make further representations, and I welcome all comments on that point. Diolch yn fawr.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text: Well, what a disappointing statement. Anyone who has walked along the Berwyn mountains, as I have done, will know how unique and special an environment it is: Cadair Berwyn, Llyn Lluncaws, Pistyll Rhaeadr, Cyrniau Nod, to name just a few places. These are wild, remote areas, which deserve to be known better amongst the people of Wales and beyond.
documents.text_cy: Wel, am ddatganiad siomedig. Bydd unrhyw un sydd wedi cerdded ar hyd mynyddoedd y Berwyn, fel dwi wedi gwneud, yn gwybod amgylchedd mor unigryw ac arbennig ydy e: Cadair Berwyn, Llyn Lluncaws, Pistyll Rhaeadr, Cyrniau Nod, i enwi ond rhai mannau. Dyma leoliadau gwyllt, anghysbell, sy'n haeddu cael eu hadnabod yn well gan drwch poblogaeth Cymru a thu hwnt.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text: Just yesterday I chaired the cross-party group on outdoor activities, where there was a unanimous view around the table on how vital and underappreciated access to the countryside is. We know what the RSPB have said about Wales being one of the most nature-deprived countries in the western world, and we heard earlier, even from the Reform Member, about the importance of tourism to our economy. So, why take this decision? There is no mention of doing this in your manifesto. I don't wish to downplay the real concerns that exist around these proposals, but the place to explore them, surely, is through a public inquiry. I'd like the Minister to explain why he doesn't believe that a public inquiry is the right format for this, because it looks to me that, at this Government's first test on its ability to protect nature, it fails spectacularly, and has instead entered into some sort of unholy trinity with the Tories and Reform. Your progressive credentials look failing to me, Minister.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text: I have to admit that I'm slightly disappointed by the comments made by my colleague behind me there. I am one who has enjoyed the Berwyn range—I've run in the Berwyn mountains on occasion. I do acknowledge and agree with the Member on the points that he's made on the importance of our natural areas and the opportunity that we have as a Government to improve that. There are a number of strategies that I've highlighted in my statement today that will do exactly that: sustainable tourism, sustainable rural communities, prosperous rural communities. Those are the opportunities that we have in taking steps across Government to make improvements. That's what I want to do, and that's what's at the forefront of my mind as I move towards a decision on these issues.
documents.text_cy: Mae'n rhaid cyfaddef fy mod i fymryn yn siomedig â sylwadau fy nghyfaill o'r cefn yn fanna. Dwi'n un sydd wedi mwynhau mynyddoedd y Berwyn—dwi wedi rhedeg mynyddoedd y Berwyn ar adegau. Dwi'n cydnabod ac yn cytuno â'r Aelod ar ei bwyntiau ar bwysigrwydd ein hardaloedd naturiol a'r cyfle sydd gyda ni fel Llywodraeth i wella hynny. Mae yna sawl strategaeth dwi wedi eu hamlygu yn fy natganiad heddiw a fydd yn gwneud yn union hynny: twristiaeth gynaliadwy, cymunedau gwledig cynaliadwy, cymunedau gwledig ffyniannus. Dyna'r cyfle sydd gyda ni wrth gymryd camau reit ar draws y Llywodraeth i wella pethau. Dyna dwi am ei wneud, a dyna sydd yn pwyso ar fy meddwl i wrth symud tuag at benderfyniad ar y materion hyn.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text: Thank you. And finally, Minister, Andrew Griffin.
documents.text_cy: Diolch. Ac yn olaf, Weinidog, Andrew Griffin.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text:
Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. As a north Powys resident, I welcome the Minister's announcement today. I think he's reached a sensible conclusion, albeit provisionally, and I'm sure my constituents in the affected area will also welcome this announcement. All five local authorities, remember—all five local authorities—objected to this proposal, and there have been very real concerns from farmers, businesses and local communities.

In my role as Chair of the Public Accounts and Public Administration Committee, I'm particularly conscious of the financial pressures facing public services. Indeed, only yesterday we were examining the serious financial difficulties facing the NHS in Wales. At £11.6 million, just to establish another national park authority, before we even consider the ongoing costs, we have to question whether that's the best use of public money. Nobody's suggesting we shouldn't protect our countryside, but, surely, we should make better use of the arrangements we already have, rather than creating another layer of bureaucracy. So, Minister, can you reassure those communities that their concerns will be properly reflected in the final decision, and tell us how quickly that decision will be made once the four weeks are up? Diolch.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text: I thank the Member. I can give that reassurance to communities. I can give that reassurance to everyone who will be submitting comments during that four-week period. I have committed to the Senedd to aim to give a final decision by Christmas, and that is my commitment to the Senedd. I believe that minimises the risk of uncertainty and disruption that these proposals have created to communities right across the area affected.

documents.item: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution: The next steps for the Glyndŵr National Park (Designation) Order
documents.text: Thank you very much, Cabinet Minister.
documents.text_cy: Diolch yn fawr iawn, Weinidog Cabinet.

documents.item: 4. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability: Winter preparedness: Be flood ready
documents.text: We'll move now to a statement by the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability: winter preparedness—be flood ready. I call on the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability, Llyr Gruffydd.
documents.text_cy: Symudwn ymlaen at ddatganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd: parodrwydd ar gyfer y gaeaf—barod am lifogydd. Galwaf ar y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd, Llyr Gruffydd.

documents.item: 4. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability: Winter preparedness: Be flood ready
documents.text:
Thank you very much, Dirprwy Lywydd. The summer of 2026, as we all know, was the warmest on record in Wales, and the drought conditions affected large parts of the country. But now we are entering the winter period, and climate change will bring wetter winters and heavier rainfall, and we are operating in an increasingly complex environment. And so we are working closely with partners to prepare for the months ahead.

Climate change is increasing both the likelihood and the severity of emergencies. This places growing pressure on our emergency responders and our risk management authorities. I'd like to thank those emergency services, Natural Resources Wales, the local authorities and others for their dedicated efforts to help keep our communities safe throughout the year.
documents.text_cy:
Diolch yn fawr iawn, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Haf 2026, fel rŷn ni'n ei wybod, oedd y cynhesaf erioed yng Nghymru, ac fe effeithiodd y sychder ar rannau helaeth o'r wlad. Ond nawr mae'r gaeaf yn agosáu, ac mi fydd newid hinsawdd yn arwain at aeafau gwlypach a glaw trymach, ac rŷn ni'n gweithio mewn amgylchedd sy'n mynd yn fwy ac yn fwy cymhleth. Ac felly rŷn ni'n gweithio'n agos â phartneriaid i baratoi ar gyfer y misoedd sydd i ddod.

Mae newid hinsawdd yn cynyddu tebygolrwydd ac yn cynyddu difrifoldeb argyfyngau. Mae hyn yn rhoi pwysau cynyddol ar ein hymatebwyr brys a'n hawdurdodau rheoli risg. Mi hoffwn i ddiolch i'r gwasanaethau brys, Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru, yr awdurdodau lleol ac eraill am eu hymdrechion ymroddedig i helpu i gadw ein cymunedau ni'n ddiogel drwy gydol y flwyddyn.

documents.item: 4. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability: Winter preparedness: Be flood ready
documents.text:
For example, this year Natural Resources Wales updated flood risk mapping at eight river locations across Wales. They also delivered improvements to their live flood warning service. NRW flood warnings and severe weather warnings are now available on a greater number of third-party digital platforms. This will therefore, of course, increase the visibility of NRW flood warnings, supporting public awareness.

As a Government, we have made almost £5 million of revenue funding available to local authorities for flood risk activities. Across Wales, they are preparing for the winter months. This includes assessing key assets, jetting drains and managing vegetation to reduce blockage risks. They are also reviewing emergency response arrangements to ensure that they remain effective.

Our national security and resilience team continues to monitor and assess all risks over the winter, including winter weather. It works with resilience partners to ensure that there's a shared understanding to support informed resilience planning across Wales.

This year, as always, our preparations are grounded in the lessons learned from previous storms. Last November, storm Claudia brought significant rainfall across Wales. The storm impacted almost 400 properties in Monmouthshire alone. Some locations saw flood depths of more than 1.5m. Communities, infrastructure and essential services were disrupted.

I understand how devastating flooding can be for households and businesses. In August of this year, I visited Milford Haven, where I heard first-hand from residents affected by flooding and discussed plans for a new flood scheme to better protect their properties. It was a powerful reminder of why this work matters.

So, let me highlight some of the ways in which we will, as a Government, support our communities and partners. We are giving flood-affected communities a stronger voice through a new independent Welsh flood forum. The new forum will support communities recovering from flooding and will strengthen preparedness and resilience for future events. It will be based on the successful model implemented in Scotland, and I can confirm that the forum’s steering group met for the first time last week. It brought together people with lived experience of flooding and partner organisations. Collectively, they will help shape a new national support network for flood-affected communities. 

We will also shortly appoint additional members to the flood and coastal erosion committee, ensuring it can continue to provide independent advice to Welsh Ministers and, in so doing, help us to shape future policy.

This Government understands the importance of continued investment in our flood risk management infrastructure, making over £85 million available in this year alone. This funding will support communities by delivering interventions ranging from flood defences to community engagement activities. It will also provide long-term flood protection and support increased resilience to climate change. Examples include schemes at Edward Street in Ystrad Mynach; Maesyffynnon Lane in Rhondda Cynon Taf; Llandysul and Pont Tyweli in Carmarthenshire; School Bank Road in Llanrwst; and Bontnewydd in Gwynedd.

Wherever possible, we encourage risk management authorities to consider investment in natural flood management interventions. These interventions complement the natural environment and help slow the movement of water through catchments, whilst improving water quality and strengthening biodiversity. Interventions can then be targeted where they are most effective, not only for communities but also for the environment.

But natural flood management can only succeed through strong partnership working with farmers and landowners. The sustainable farming scheme will be an important part of this. It will help land managers to adopt nature-based solutions, which reduce flood risk and support wider environmental and climate resilience outcomes. However, despite this continued investment, it is essential that communities remain vigilant to the risk of flooding and are prepared for all eventualities. One in seven properties in Wales is at risk of flooding, but only 27 per cent of those householders are registered to receive NRW's flood warnings.

This week, NRW is running its annual Be Flood Ready campaign. Many of you will perhaps have seen that on social media in recent days. The campaign highlights three simple steps that everyone can take to be better prepared for flooding. Firstly, you should check your property's flood risk, and you can do that online. NRW's website allows people to check flood-risk information using their postcode and an interactive map. Secondly, then sign up for free flood warnings, from both rivers and the sea. Warnings can be received via text messages, e-mail or voicemail messages, and people can register through NRW's website or by contacting Floodline, and I will share the number: it's 0345 988 1188. And finally, be prepared when flooding is forecast. NRW provides practical online advice to help people prepare for, to respond to, and then, of course, to recover from flooding. And I encourage everyone to make use of these free resources. Please do check if you or your family are at risk of flooding, and, if you are, please then access all the support available to you.

I also encourage everyone to review their insurance arrangements. Flood cover is not always included in standard household insurance policies. It is therefore important to check the details of your cover. Some new policies may not take effect immediately, so acting early can be crucial in that regard. And for those who find it difficult to obtain cover, I would like to highlight two specific schemes. The first is Flood Re. This UK-wide scheme helps households access affordable flood insurance, and it may be particularly relevant, of course, to people who have previously experienced flooding or who have struggled to obtain insurance cover. The Flood Re website provides details of participating insurers, but I encourage people to consider their options carefully. And the second is the build back better scheme. This allows householders recovering from flooding to install flood resilience measures in their property during the repair process, and up to £10,000 may be available from insurers to support these improvements.

But in looking ahead, Dirprwy Lywydd, preparation remains our strongest defence against flooding and severe weather. The Welsh Government will continue to work closely with partners to strengthen resilience, to learn, of course, from past events, and to support our communities, and I want to thank everyone involved in that work. By working together, we can help ensure that Wales is ready for the challenges this winter may bring. Thank you.
documents.text_cy:
Er enghraifft, eleni fe ddiweddarodd Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru fapiau perygl llifogydd mewn wyth lleoliad afonydd ledled y wlad. Fe wnaethon nhw hefyd gyflwyno gwelliannau i'w gwasanaeth rhybuddio byw am lifogydd. Mae rhybuddion llifogydd Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru a rhybuddion tywydd garw bellach ar gael ar fwy o lwyfannau digidol trydydd parti. Mi fydd hyn felly, wrth gwrs, yn cynyddu gwelededd rhybuddion llifogydd Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru, gan gefnogi ymwybyddiaeth y cyhoedd.

Fel Llywodraeth, rŷn ni wedi sicrhau bod £5 miliwn o gyllid refeniw ar gael i awdurdodau lleol ar gyfer gweithgareddau perygl llifogydd. Ledled Cymru, maen nhw'n paratoi ar gyfer misoedd y gaeaf. Mae hyn yn cynnwys asesu asedau allweddol, jetio draeniau a rheoli llystyfiant i leihau'r risg bod draeniau'n cael eu blocio. Maen nhw hefyd yn adolygu trefniadau ymateb brys i sicrhau eu bod nhw'n parhau i fod yn effeithiol.

Mae ein tîm diogelwch a gwydnwch cenedlaethol yn parhau i fonitro ac asesu'r holl risgiau dros y gaeaf, gan gynnwys tywydd y gaeaf. Mae'n gweithio gyda phartneriaid gwydnwch i sicrhau bod dealltwriaeth gyffredin i gefnogi cynllunio gwybodus i wella gwydnwch ledled Cymru.

Eleni, fel bob amser, mae ein paratoadau ni wedi'u seilio ar y gwersi a ddysgwyd o stormydd blaenorol. Fis Tachwedd diwethaf, daeth storm Claudia â glawiad sylweddol ledled Cymru. Fe wnaeth y storm effeithio ar ryw 400 eiddo yn sir Fynwy yn unig. Gwelodd rai lleoliadau ddyfnderoedd llifogydd o fwy na 1.5m. Bu tarfu ar gymunedau, seilwaith a gwasanaethau hanfodol.

Dwi'n deall pa mor ddinistriol y gall llifogydd fod i aelwydydd a busnesau. Ym mis Awst eleni, fe ymwelais i ag Aberdaugleddau, lle clywais yn uniongyrchol gan drigolion yr oedd y llifogydd wedi effeithio arnyn hwy nhw a thrafod cynlluniau ar gyfer cynllun llifogydd newydd i ddiogelu eu heiddo nhw yn well. Roedd yn atgofiad pwerus o pam mae'r gwaith yma yn bwysig.

Felly, gadewch i fi dynnu sylw at rai o'r ffyrdd y byddwn ni fel Llywodraeth yn cefnogi ein cymunedau a'n partneriaid. Rŷn ni'n helpu cymunedau sydd wedi dioddef llifogydd i gael llais cryfach drwy fforwm llifogydd annibynnol newydd yma yng Nghymru. Mi fydd y fforwm newydd yn cefnogi cymunedau sy'n gwella o lifogydd ac yn cryfhau parodrwydd a gwydnwch ar gyfer digwyddiadau yn y dyfodol. Mi fydd yn seiliedig ar y model llwyddiannus a weithredwyd yn yr Alban, ac mi allaf gadarnhau bod y grŵp llywio ar gyfer y fforwm wedi cyfarfod am y tro cyntaf yr wythnos diwethaf. Mi ddaeth â phobl sydd â phrofiad bywyd o lifogydd a sefydliadau partner ynghyd. Gyda'i gilydd, mi fyddan nhw'n helpu i lunio rhwydwaith cymorth cenedlaethol newydd ar gyfer cymunedau y mae llifogydd wedi effeithio arnyn nhw.

Mi fyddwn ni hefyd yn penodi aelodau ychwanegol i'r pwyllgor llifogydd ac erydu arfordirol cyn bo hir, gan sicrhau y gall barhau i roi cyngor annibynnol i Weinidogion Cymru a, thrwy wneud hynny, ein helpu ni i lunio polisi yn y dyfodol.

Mae'r Llywodraeth hon yn deall pwysigrwydd buddsoddiad parhaus yn ein seilwaith rheoli perygl llifogydd, gan sicrhau bod dros £85 miliwn ar gael eleni yn unig. Bydd y cynllun yn cefnogi cymunedau drwy gyflwyno ymyriadau sy'n amrywio o amddiffynfeydd rhag llifogydd i weithgareddau ymgysylltu â'r gymuned. Mi fydd yn darparu amddiffyniad rhag llifogydd hirdymor ac, wrth gwrs, yn gwella ein gallu i wrthsefyll newid hinsawdd. Mae enghreifftiau'n cynnwys cynlluniau yn Edward Street yn Ystrad Mynach; Maesyffynnon Lane yn Rhondda Cynon Taf; Llandysul a Phont Tyweli yn sir Gaerfyrddin; School Bank Road yn Llanrwst; a'r Bontnewydd yng Ngwynedd.

Lle bynnag y bo'n bosibl, rŷn ni'n annog awdurdodau rheoli risg i ystyried buddsoddi mewn ymyriadau rheoli llifogydd naturiol. Mae'r ymyriadau hyn yn ategu'r amgylchedd naturiol ac yn helpu i arafu symudiad dŵr trwy ddalgylchoedd, neu catchments, gan wella ansawdd dŵr ar yr un pryd a chryfhau bioamrywiaeth hefyd. Mae modd targedu ymyriadau lle maen nhw'n fwyaf effeithiol, nid yn unig i'r gymuned ond hefyd i'r amgylchedd.

Ond dim ond trwy weithio mewn partneriaeth gref gyda ffermwyr a thirfeddianwyr y gall dulliau naturiol o reoli llifogydd fel hyn lwyddo ar eu gorau. Mi fydd y cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy yn rhan bwysig o hyn. Mi fydd yn helpu rheolwyr tir i fabwysiadu atebion sy'n seiliedig ar natur, sy'n lleihau'r perygl o lifogydd ac yn cefnogi canlyniadau ehangach o wydnwch amgylcheddol a hinsawdd. Fodd bynnag, er gwaethaf y buddsoddiad parhaus yma i gyd, mae'n hanfodol bod cymunedau'n parhau i fod yn wyliadwrus i'r risg o lifogydd ac, wrth gwrs, i fod yn barod ar gyfer pob posibilrwydd. Mae un o bob saith eiddo yng Nghymru mewn perygl o lifogydd, a dim ond 27 y cant o'r deiliaid tai hynny sydd wedi'u cofrestru i dderbyn rhybuddion llifogydd gan Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru.

Yr wythnos hon, mae Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru yn cynnal ei ymgyrch flynyddol Barod am Lifogydd. Mae'n bosib bod nifer ohonoch chi wedi gweld hynny ar y cyfryngau yn y dyddiau diwethaf. Mae'r ymgyrch yn tynnu sylw at dri cham syml y gall pawb eu cymryd i baratoi'n well ar gyfer llifogydd. Yn gyntaf, mi ddylech chi wirio risg llifogydd eich eiddo, ac fe allwch chi wneud hynny ar-lein. Mae gwefan Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru yn caniatáu i bobl wirio gwybodaeth am risg llifogydd gan ddefnyddio eu cod post a map rhyngweithiol. Yn ail wedyn, cofrestrwch i gael rhybuddion am ddim o lifogydd o afonydd a'r môr. Mae modd cael rhybuddion trwy neges destun, trwy e-bost neu neges llais, ac mi all pobl gofrestru drwy wefan Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru neu drwy gysylltu â Floodline, ac mi wnaf ddweud y rhif: 0345 988 1188. Ac yn olaf wedyn, byddwch yn barod pan fo rhagolygon o lifogydd. Mae Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru yn darparu cymorth ymarferol ar-lein i helpu pobl i baratoi ar gyfer llifogydd, ond hefyd i ymateb iddyn nhw, ac wedyn, wrth gwrs, i adfer ar eu hôl nhw. Dwi'n annog pawb i ddefnyddio'r adnoddau yma sy'n rhad ac am ddim i bob un. Gwiriwch a ydych chi neu'ch teulu mewn perygl o lifogydd, ac, os ydych chi, sicrhewch eich bod chi'n cael mynediad at yr holl gymorth sydd ar gael.

Dwi hefyd yn annog pawb i adolygu eu trefniadau yswiriant. Dyw yswiriant llifogydd ddim bob amser wedi'i gynnwys mewn polisïau yswiriant cartref safonol. Felly, mae'n bwysig gwirio manylion eich yswiriant. Efallai na fydd rhai polisïau newydd yn dod i rym ar unwaith, felly gall gweithredu'n gynnar fod yn hanfodol yn hynny o beth hefyd. Ac i'r rhai sy'n ei chael hi'n anodd cael yswiriant, wel, mi hoffwn i dynnu sylw at ddau gynllun penodol. Y cyntaf yw Flood Re. Mae'r cynllun hwn, sy'n gweithredu ledled y Deyrnas Unedig, yn helpu aelwydydd i gael mynediad at yswiriant llifogydd fforddiadwy, ac mi all hyn fod yn arbennig o berthnasol, wrth gwrs, i bobl sydd wedi profi llifogydd o'r blaen neu wedi cael trafferth cael yswiriant. Mae gwefan Flood Re yn darparu manylion yswirwyr sy'n cymryd rhan yn y cynllun, ond dwi'n annog pobl i ystyried eu dewisiadau yn ofalus. A'r ail wedyn yw'r cynllun ailgodi'n gryfach. Nawr, mae hyn yn caniatáu i ddeiliaid tai sy'n adfer ar ôl llifogydd i osod mesurau gwydnwch llifogydd yn eu heiddo yn ystod y broses o atgyweirio, ac efallai y bydd hyd at £10,000 ar gael gan yswirwyr i gefnogi'r gwelliannau hyn.

Ond wrth edrych ymlaen, Ddirprwy Lywydd, paratoi yw'r ffordd orau o amddiffyn ein hunain rhag llifogydd a thywydd eithafol. Mi fydd Llywodraeth Cymru'n parhau i weithio'n agos â phartneriaid i'n gwneud ni'n fwy gwydn, i ddysgu, wrth gwrs, o ddigwyddiadau blaenorol a hefyd i gefnogi ein cymunedau, ac mi hoffwn i ddiolch i bawb sy'n rhan o'r gwaith hwnnw. Drwy gydweithio, fe allwn ni helpu i sicrhau bod Cymru'n barod ar gyfer yr heriau y gallem ni eu hwynebu'r gaeaf hwn. Diolch yn fawr.

documents.item: 4. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability: Winter preparedness: Be flood ready
documents.text:
Thank you for your statement, Minister. Natural Resources Wales has warned of a higher risk of flooding this year than last year, with one in seven homes and businesses in Wales at risk. People are being told to prepare, but what your Government has outlined today just doesn't cut it, sadly, and fails to reassure those affected by flooding year on year. We already know where the flooding will be. Communities are already doing everything they can to prepare, but I do agree that there does need to be greater awareness of tools that are available to alert to flood warnings. But, across the border, the Government has set out £4.2 billion for flood defences and also set out what emergency resources they will provide, including 260 mobile pumps, 250 km of temporary barriers and so on.
