Ac felly, mae angen edrych yn fanwl iawn, fel mae'n cyfaill y Gweinidog Cabinet dros iechyd wedi'i wneud, ar beth yn union yw'r cynlluniau. Ydyn nhw'n gynlluniau sy'n mynd i ddelifro i'r tymor hir? Ydyn nhw'n sicrhau bod yna gydweithio rhwng y gwasanaeth iechyd a'r gwasanaeth gofal trwy awdurdodau lleol i sicrhau bod y pecyn gofal yn gyflawn, i sicrhau bod rhai o'r heriau sydd yn y system yn cael eu hannerch? Ydyn nhw'n edrych, fel y gwnaeth fy nghydweithwraig gynnau fach gyfeirio atyn nhw, i'r hirdymor gyda'r gweithlu? Mae'r holl faterion yna'n gorfod dod at ei gilydd, a gofyn y cwestiwn bob tro: ydy'r arian yma yn mynd i wneud newid go iawn yn yr hirdymor, nid jest am y tymor byr? Diolch yn fawr.

documents.text: Thank you. Before moving on to the next question—
documents.text_cy: Diolch. Cyn symud ymlaen i'r cwestiwn nesaf—

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: —can I just remind Members of the conventions, protocols, guidelines and otherwise in this Chamber of not accusing or coming close to accusing other Members of lying or misleading? There are points of debate, but we have ways of debating this within the Chamber. It's not aimed at anybody in particular. In the generality, please, abide by that.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: 6. What assessment has the Welsh Government made of the need for a new Wales Act to ensure equality of powers with Scotland? OQ64630
documents.text_cy: 6. Pa asesiad y mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi'i wneud o'r angen am Ddeddf Cymru newydd i sicrhau pwerau sy'n gyfartal â'r Alban? OQ64630

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: Our assessment is that Wales should have the powers that it needs to deliver for the people of Wales, improve services and strengthen accountability. We are pressing for a fairer settlement for Wales. A new Wales Bill would provide the clearest way and the most effective way of implementing agreed changes.
documents.text_cy: Ein hasesiad ni yw y dylai Cymru gael y pwerau sydd eu hangen i gyflawni dros bobl Cymru, gwella gwasanaethau a chryfhau atebolrwydd. Rŷn ni yn pwyso am setliad tecach i Gymru. Byddai Bil Cymru newydd yn darparu'r ffordd gliriaf a mwyaf effeithiol o wneud y newidiadau y cytunir arnynt.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: Thank you for that response. The current devolution settlement in Wales leaves us short of many of the powers and the flexibility that we need as a nation to formulate and implement coherent cross-departmental policies for the benefit of our communities. I was very pleased to hear the First Minister of Wales announce last week that he had written to the UK Prime Minister formally to try to secure a new deal for Wales, a deal that would transfer a number of powers that have already been devolved to Scotland, such as policing, justice, the Crown Estate, railways, welfare and fiscal fairness. A number of independent commissions and reviews over the years, including the Silk commission and the Independent Commission on the Constitutional Future of Wales, have come to the conclusion that devolution needs to be strengthened and more powers placed in the hands of the Senedd in order to allow Wales to deal more effectively with its own challenges. With that in mind, will the Cabinet Minister commit to continuing to press the UK Government? Finally—
documents.text_cy: Diolch am yr ymateb. Mae'r setliad datganoli presennol yng Nghymru yn ein gadael ni'n fyr o nifer o'r pwerau a'r hyblygrwydd sydd eu hangen arnom fel cenedl i lunio a gweithredu polisïau trawsadrannol, cydlynol er lles ein cymunedau. Roeddwn i'n falch iawn o glywed Prif Weinidog Cymru yn cyhoeddi'r wythnos diwethaf ei fod wedi ysgrifennu at Brif Weinidog y Deyrnas Unedig yn ffurfiol i geisio sicrhau bargen newydd i Gymru, bargen fyddai'n trosglwyddo nifer o'r pwerau sydd eisoes wedi'u datganoli i'r Alban, megis plismona, cyfiawnder, Ystad y Goron, rheilffyrdd, lles a thegwch ariannol. Mae nifer o gomisiynau annibynnol dros y blynyddoedd, gan gynnwys comisiwn Silk a'r Comisiwn Annibynnol ar Ddyfodol Cyfansoddiadol Cymru, wedi dod i'r casgliad bod angen cryfhau datganoli a rhoi mwy o bwerau yn nwylo'r Senedd er mwyn galluogi Cymru i fynd i'r afael yn fwy effeithiol â'u heriau ei hun. Gyda hynny mewn golwg, a wnaiff y Gweinidog Cabinet ymrwymo i barhau i bwyso ar Lywodraeth y Deyrnas Unedig? O'r diwedd—

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: Cabinet Minister.
documents.text_cy: Gweinidog Cabinet.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: Thank you. I believe the Member is asking me to commit to press the UK Government to secure progress. I make that clear commitment this afternoon, and I do so happily. I think it's worth reporting to the Senedd that my initial meetings with UK Cabinet Ministers have been constructive and collaborative. Of course, as the discussions develop, we will get into the minutiae. But I am eager to emphasise that the response that I've received to date has been positive, and I therefore hope that that will be the basis for further progress.
documents.text_cy: Diolch yn fawr. Dwi'n credu bod yr Aelod yn gofyn i fi ymrwymo i bwyso ar Lywodraeth Prydain i sicrhau cynnydd. Dwi'n gwneud yr ymrwymiad hwnnw yn glir ac yn hapus. Dwi'n credu ei bod hi'n werth adrodd wrth y Senedd fod fy nghyfarfodydd cychwynnol i gyda Gweinidogion Cabinet o Lywodraeth Prydain wedi bod yn adeiladol ac yn gydweithredol. Wrth gwrs, wrth i'r trafodaethau fynd yn eu blaen, fe ddown ni i mewn i'r manylion. Ond dwi yn awyddus i bwysleisio bod yr ymateb sydd wedi dod hyd yn hyn wedi bod yn gadarnhaol, ac felly dwi'n gobeithio y bydd hynny yn sail i gynnydd pellach.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: 7. What action is the Welsh Government taking to decentralise decision making within Wales? OQ64636
documents.text_cy: 7. Pa gamau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i ddatganoli gwneud penderfyniadau o fewn Cymru? OQ64636

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: The Welsh Government will work closely with partners at a local and regional level to ensure that decision making and service delivery take place in ways that support effective delivery of public services.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: Thank you for that answer. Andy Burnham, the new Prime Minister, of course, has set out his ambition to rewire the state. It's quite clear to me and many people in Wales that we need to rewire Wales in order to make sure that people in their communities have a greater opportunity to shape the decisions that are made about those communities by politicians at all levels. One of the ways to do that is to make politicians more accountable to the citizens that they serve. What action is the Welsh Government going to take to address the accountability gap created by the new Senedd election system, which, I'm afraid, the way that it is at the moment, does not give an opportunity for individual members of the public to demonstrate their support for an individual candidate, rather than a political party?

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: Well, I'm delighted to see that the Welsh Conservatives are now in favour of the single transferrable vote. I should encourage everyone—[Interruption.] I should encourage everyone in this—[Interruption.] Well, that is the best way—[Interruption.] That is the best way—[Interruption.] That is the best way to ensure effective accountability, and I hope in due course that every Member of the Senedd will support such a development of the Welsh electoral system.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: 8. What is the Government's approach to ensuring co-operation across portfolios to deliver the Programme for Government? OQ64627
documents.text_cy: 8. Sut mae’r Llywodraeth yn mynd ati i sicrhau cydweithio traws-portffolio i gyflawni'r Rhaglen Lywodraethu? OQ64627

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: The greatest challenges facing Wales demand a whole-Government response. That is why our programme for government sets out a new ambition for Wales, based on shared priorities rather than departmental silos. I work closely with colleagues right across the Cabinet to ensure that the Government collaborates across portfolios to ensure meaningful outcomes for people across Wales.
documents.text_cy: Mae'r heriau mwyaf sy'n wynebu Cymru yn galw am ymateb ar draws y Llywodraeth gyfan. Dyna pam mae ein rhaglen lywodraethu yn nodi uchelgais newydd i Gymru, wedi'i seilio ar flaenoriaethau a rennir yn hytrach nag ar seilos adrannol. Dwi'n gweithio'n agos iawn gyda chydweithwyr reit ar draws y Cabinet i sicrhau bod y Llywodraeth yn cydweithio ar draws portffolios er mwyn sicrhau canlyniadau ystyrlon i bobl ledled Cymru.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: Thank you, Minister. I was delighted to lead a debate in this Chamber on the need to integrate the work of preventing ACEs, or adverse childhood experiences, and respond to them across public services. The experience of a child or a person of trauma doesn't respect departmental boundaries. Housing, health, education, social care and employment can all play their part in creating conditions where children and families recover from trauma and prosper. Will you therefore outline how the Government will help to ensure that trauma and adverse experiences during childhood, or ACEs, are covered across Government, rather than as an issue for individual departments?
documents.text_cy: Diolch, Weinidog. Roeddwn i'n falch iawn o arwain dadl yn y Siambr hon am yr angen i integreiddio'r gwaith o atal ACEs, neu adverse childhood experiences, ac ymateb iddynt ar draws gwasanaethau cyhoeddus. Nid yw profiad plentyn neu berson o drawma yn parchu ffiniau adrannol. Gall tai, addysg, iechyd, gofal cymdeithasol a chyflogaeth oll chwarae rhan mewn creu amodau ble mae plant a theuluoedd yn adfer o drawma ac yn ffynnu. A wnewch chi felly amlinellu sut y bydd y Llywodraeth yn helpu i sicrhau bod trawma a phrofiadau niweidiol yn ystod plentyndod, ACEs, yn cael sylw ar draws y Llywodraeth, yn hytrach nag fel mater i adrannau unigol?

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text:
I thank the Member for the question, and I pay tribute to the work that she has carried out, and others in the Chamber, on a cross-party basis, to develop our understanding of the impact that trauma does have on children and, indeed, on adults who have experienced trauma as children. Through the trauma-informed Wales framework and the support of ACE Hub Wales and close collaboration across ministerial portfolios, we're implementing approaches informed by adverse childhood experiences and trauma across the development of policies and the provision of services.

Preventing ACEs and responding effectively to trauma is a responsibility that's shared across the Government and public services. Our approach has been planned to ensure that the work is co-ordinated, rather than left to individual organisations and departments to implement themselves. That's our ambition, Llywydd. My hope as part of my role is to ensure that that does happen. That ambition, which was shared by Governments of the past, hasn't always been implemented at grass-roots level, and that's what I would wish to focus on.
documents.text_cy:
Diolch yn fawr iawn i'r Aelod am y cwestiwn, a dwi'n talu teyrnged i'r gwaith mae hi wedi'i wneud, ac eraill yn y Siambr hon, ar sail drawsbleidiol, i ddatblygu ein dealltwriaeth ni o'r effaith mae trawma yn ei gael ar blant ac, yn wir, ar y sawl sy'n oedolion sydd wedi profi trawma yn blant. Trwy fframwaith Cymru sy'n ystyriol o drawma, cefnogaeth Hyb ACE Cymru a chydweithio agos ar draws portffolios gweinidogol, rŷm ni'n ymgorffori dulliau sy'n ystyriol o adverse childhood experiences a thrawma ar draws datblygu polisïau a darparu gwasanaethau.

Mae atal profiadau niweidiol yn ystod plentyndod ac ymateb yn effeithiol i drawma yn gyfrifoldeb a rennir ar draws y Llywodraeth a gwasanaethau cyhoeddus. Mae'n ddull gweithredu wedi ei gynllunio i sicrhau bod y gwaith yn cael ei gydlynu, yn hytrach na'i adael i adrannau a sefydliadau unigol i weithredu ar eu pennau eu hunain. Dyna'n huchelgais, Lywydd. Fy ngobaith i fel rhan o fy rôl i yw sicrhau bod hynny'n digwydd. Mae'r uchelgais honno, sydd wedi'i rhannu gan Lywodraethau yn y gorffennol, heb o reidrwydd bob tro wedi cael ei gweithredu ar lawr gwlad, a dyna fyddwn i'n dymuno canolbwyntio arno.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: Question 9 was grouped with question 5. Question 10 [OQ64637] is withdrawn. So, question 11, Steven Rodaway.
documents.text_cy: Mae cwestiwn 9 wedi ei grwpio gyda cwestiwn 5. Cwestiwn 10 [OQ64637] tynnwyd yn ôl. Felly, cwestiwn 11, Steven Rodaway.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: Thank you, Llywydd.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: 11. What discussions has the Cabinet Minister had with the UK Minister for Policing and the Secretary of State for Wales regarding the devolution of policing? OQ64634
documents.text_cy: 11. Pa drafodaethau y mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet wedi'u cael gyda Gweinidog Plismona y DU ac Ysgrifennydd Gwladol Cymru ynglŷn â datganoli plismona? OQ64634

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: This Government’s position is clear: policing should be fully devolved to Wales. The Dirprwy Brif Weinidog and I have met with the policing Minister to discuss devolution and other policing priorities. I've also had an introductory meeting with the Secretary of State for Wales.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text:
Thank you. Minister, your Government's supplementary budget was recently defeated. Your finance Minister then wrote

'we must avoid creating additional spending obligations where the funding position has yet to be agreed.'

Before seeking more policing powers, your Government should demonstrate that it can deliver with the powers it already holds. Education is devolved, yet Wales has the worst Programme for International Student Assessment scores in the United Kingdom.

Your Government is also struggling with other existing responsibilities, such as cutting NHS waiting lists. Your own statistics show that the number of pathways waiting for treatment increased between June and July, with two-year waits also rising. Those are delivery problems under responsibilities you already hold. And yet, with all these current issues the Government is struggling with, surprisingly, you seek additional devolved powers for policing. Money doesn't grow on trees, although our previous Welsh Government seemed to test that theory in Uganda. Given your record of failings, what evidence do you have that this Government can deliver if policing is devolved? Thank you.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text:
I thank the Member for the question. I'm not entirely sure that he is convinced of a record of failings after five months. I should probably remind him that another party was in Government for 27 years, and if he wants to address—[Interruption.] If he wants to address questions to Members of that party, I'm sure he can do so afterwards in the tea room.

Our focus as a Government is on delivery, on schools, on childcare, on child poverty, on the NHS and on the economy. We have identified that there is a programme of policing reform taking place now for the England and Wales jurisdiction, led by the Home Office. There is an opportunity there to make the case for greater devolution for Wales, for greater responsibility for the Welsh Government, which will make communities in Wales safer, and that is what we will pursue.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: 12. How is the Welsh Government ensuring the successful implementation of the Well‑being of Future Generations (Wales) Act 2015? OQ64623
documents.text_cy: 12. Sut mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn sicrhau bod Deddf Llesiant Cenedlaethau'r Dyfodol (Cymru) 2015 yn cael ei gweithredu'n llwyddiannus? OQ64623

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: The programme for government and our well-being objectives are a single framework for action, linking the priorities people have entrusted us to deliver and the long-term outcomes of the Act that we want to achieve. I've also agreed to a review of the Act, focusing on enhancing the Act’s implementation in practice.
documents.text_cy: Mae’r rhaglen lywodraethu a'n hamcanion llesiant yn un fframwaith gweithredu sy’n cysylltu'r blaenoriaethau mae pobl wedi ymddiried ynom i’w cyflawni a’r canlyniadau hirdymor yn y Ddeddf rydym am eu cyflawni. Dwi hefyd wedi cytuno i adolygiad o'r Ddeddf, gan ganolbwyntio ar wella’r ffordd mae’r Ddeddf yn cael ei gweithredu.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: Minister, culture has faced a decade of funding cuts. Funding cuts don't just affect the arts sector. They also have a direct impact on the well-being and vitality of Welsh communities and society. If we are serious about the well-being of future generations Act, we must ring-fence and protect preventative funding to support the arts. Culture contributes directly to the well-being of individuals and to the vitality of our communities throughout Wales. So, how will the Minister work across portfolios to ensure that culture is recognised as an integral part of preventative health across Government?
documents.text_cy: Weinidog, mae diwylliant wedi wynebu degawd o doriadau cyllid. Nid yw toriadau i gyllid yn effeithio ar y sector celfyddydol yn unig. Maent hefyd yn cael effaith uniongyrchol ar lesiant a bywiogrwydd cymunedau a chymdeithas Cymru. Os ydym am fod o ddifrif ynghylch Deddf llesiant cenedlaethau'r dyfodol, rhaid neilltuo a diogelu cyllid ataliol i gefnogi'r celfyddydau. Mae diwylliant yn cyfrannu'n uniongyrchol at lesiant unigolion ac at fywiogrwydd ein cymunedau ledled Cymru. Felly, sut y bydd y Gweinidog yn gweithio ar draws portffolios i sicrhau bod diwylliant yn cael ei gydnabod fel rhan annatod o iechyd ataliol ar draws y Llywodraeth?

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: I thank the Member for that question. There is a clear commitment from this Government to promote culture and sport. There is a new culture and sport strategy, which is being led by the Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport and Trefnydd. There is a clear focus from this Government on promoting sport and culture, whilst also recognising, as you have set out, the important role that culture and sport can have across a range of public policies, including the preventative health agenda, which is hugely important to this Government. Thank you.
documents.text_cy: Diolch yn fawr i'r Aelod am y cwestiwn. Mae yna ymrwymiad clir gan y Llywodraeth yma i hybu diwylliant a chwaraeon. Mae yna strategaeth diwylliant a chwaraeon newydd dan ofal y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon a'r Trefnydd. Mae yna ffocws clir gan y Llywodraeth hon ar hybu a hyrwyddo chwaraeon a diwylliant, ond hefyd cydnabod, fel rŷch chi wedi nodi, y rôl bwysig mae diwylliant a chwaraeon yn gallu ei chael ar draws ystod polisi cyhoeddus, gan gynnwys yr agenda iechyd ataliol, sy'n bwysig iawn i'r Llywodraeth hon. Diolch yn fawr.

documents.item: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
documents.text: Thank you very much, Minister.
documents.text_cy: Diolch yn fawr i chi, Weinidog.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: We will move now to item 3, the business statement and announcement, and I call on the Trefnydd, Heledd Fychan.
documents.text_cy: Symudwn ymlaen i eitem 3, datganiad a chyhoeddiad busnes. Galwaf ar y Trefnydd, Heledd Fychan.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Thank you, Dirprwy Lywydd. There are no changes to this week's business. Draft Plenary business for the next three weeks is shown on the business statement, which is available to Members electronically.
documents.text_cy: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Nid oes unrhyw newidiadau i fusnes yr wythnos hon. Mae busnes drafft y tair wythnos nesaf wedi'i nodi yn y datganiad busnes, sydd ar gael i holl Aelodau'n electronig.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Minister, I would like an urgent statement on who is holding the Welsh Ambulance Services University NHS Trust to account for electrification and decarbonisation spending. My freedom of information request remains unanswered. Financial information requested before our future meeting is being withheld. This is public money, and that is unacceptable. Is this yet another expensive vanity project with little obvious tangible benefits to patients? Where's the funded plan? What evidence shows this spending will cut response times, deliver life-saving treatment sooner and save lives, or will this ultimately cost lives on the altar of decarbonisation? Can the Minister guarantee those improvements? If so, show the Chamber credible evidence from an independent body. If the ambulance service persists with this project, will the Minister restore the previous response time measure alongside current reporting so that the public can accurately judge performance? Saving lives must be the measure of success. Thank you.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: There are questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care tomorrow, so it would be appropriate for you to raise them tomorrow during that session. If there's no opportunity to do that, I would suggest that you write with all of your questions to the Minister directly.
documents.text_cy: Mae yna gwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal yfory, felly fe fyddai'n briodol i chi fod yn codi'r rhain yn ystod y sesiwn honno. Os na fydd yna gyfle, mi fuaswn i'n awgrymu eich bod chi'n ysgrifennu gyda'ch holl gwestiynau at y Gweinidog yn uniongyrchol.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Could I ask for a statement from the Government updating us on the work on the fire summit, please? I know that there was a very clear consensus in the Chamber when we had the statement from the First Minister that there should be involvement of those who worked at a grass-roots level—so, farmers and others who supported the firefighters in their efforts. I was concerned to see that, of the representatives from Blaenavon, just one has been included. Indeed, one of the key landowners has actually been uninvited. I'm also informed that the summit is only going to be for two hours. I would question whether that will be enough to deal with something as significant as this. So, could I ask the Trefnydd whether we could have an update on this?

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Thank you for raising those issues. You will have heard the First Minister stating unambiguously the commitment of this Government to look at and learn the necessary lessons from those experiences. You will also know the order of business in this Senedd. With the concerns that you expresses, I would suggest that writing to the First Minister would be best, because they were very specific issues that you raised. I think, in looking at the business programme, perhaps there wouldn't be space for such a statement for a number of weeks, whereas the issues that you have raised suggest that you need an answer sooner than that. Clearly, we are committed to continuing to update this Senedd and we will do so with all Members on this crucial issue.
documents.text_cy: Diolch i chi am godi'r materion hynny. Mi fyddwch chi wedi clywed y Prif Weinidog yn gyfan gwbl ddiamwys o ran ymroddiad y Llywodraeth hon i fod yn edrych a dysgu'r gwersi angenrheidiol o hynny. Mi fyddwch chi'n gwybod hefyd trefn busnes y Senedd hon. Gyda'r pryderon rydych chi'n eu codi, mi fuaswn yn awgrymu mai ysgrifennu at y Prif Weinidog fyddai orau, gan fod yna bethau penodol iawn rydych chi wedi'u codi. Rwy'n credu, o edrych ar y rhaglen fusnes, ei bod hi'n bosibl na fydd lle am nifer o wythnosau am ddatganiad o'r fath, ac mae'r hyn rydych chi wedi'i godi yn awgrymu bod angen ateb arnoch yn gynt na hynny. Yn amlwg, rydyn ni wedi ymrwymo i barhau i ddiweddaru'r Senedd hon ac i ymwneud â phob Aelod ar y mater hollbwysig hwn.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Trefnydd, I'd like to request a statement from the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy on the announcement that Milford Haven's Impala terminal is to cease its commercial operations at the end of this year. We must fully understand the implications of this announcement, including the scale of any job losses and the impact on the local economy. We also need further clarity on how the Welsh Government intends to support both the company and its workforce as this situation develops. These are highly skilled and valuable jobs, and every effort must be made to retain this expertise within the region and to safeguard future employment opportunities. In my view, losing such skills would be a significant blow to the local economy and, indeed, to the wider energy sector. Therefore, I'd be grateful if the Welsh Government could provide an urgent statement outlining its engagement with the company to date, the discussions it has held regarding the future of the terminal and the support that may be available to both the workforce and the operator, going forward.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: I thank the Member for raising an important matter that I know is of great concern to Members in the wake of this news, and I know that the Government is in discussions with the company to understand what the implications are. I also understand that there is a topical question on this issue, which will be a matter for the Llywydd and Dirprwy Lywydd to consider. Certainly, we are very disappointed to hear this news. I know that this will create great concern locally and for those who face uncertainty in the broader community. So, I can provide that assurance to the Member that those discussions with the Government and the company are continuing and, certainly, I will ensure that the Cabinet Minister knows that you have raised this important issue today.
documents.text_cy: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi mater rwy'n gwybod sy'n pryderu nifer fawr o Aelodau yn sgil y newyddion hwn, ac rwy'n gwybod bod y Llywodraeth mewn trafodaethau â'r cwmni i ddeall beth ydy goblygiadau hyn. Dwi'n deall hefyd fod yna gwestiwn amserol ar y pwnc hwn a fydd yn fater, wrth gwrs, i'r Llywydd a'r Dirprwy Lywydd ei ystyried. Yn sicr, rydyn ni'n siomedig dros ben o glywed y newyddion hwn. Dwi'n gwybod y bydd hyn yn creu pryder aruthrol yn lleol ac i'r rheini sydd yn wynebu ansicrwydd, ynghyd â'r gymuned ehangach. Felly, rwy'n rhoi'r sicrwydd hwnnw i'r Aelod fod y trafodaethau hynny â'r Llywodraeth yn parhau, ac yn sicr mi fyddaf yn sicrhau bod y Gweinidog Cabinet yn gwybod eich bod chi wedi codi'r mater pwysig hwn gyda mi heddiw.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Trefnydd, could I request an urgent statement from the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care regarding the reported outbreak of scabies in the Hywel Dda health board area, and the adequacy of the Welsh Government's response to this developing public health concern? There is growing concern about the spread of scabies within communities and care settings. The situation has become even more alarming following the reported death of an elderly gentleman, whose illness was linked to complications associated with scabies. Given the vulnerability of older people, those living in residential care and individuals with underlying health concerns, there are serious questions about the infection control measures, the availability of treatment, support for care providers and the steps being taken to prevent further outbreaks. An urgent statement would provide an opportunity for the Welsh Government to update Members on the current scale and extent of the outbreak in west Wales, measures being taken to contain transmission and protect vulnerable individuals, guidance being provided to care homes, hospitals and community healthcare providers, and whether additional resources or support are being made available to affected areas. Given the significant public concern and the potential implications for public health, I believe that this matter warrants an urgent statement at the earliest opportunity. Diolch.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: I thank the Member for raising this issue. I do hope that you took the opportunity to write to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care. There are questions to the Minister tomorrow here in the Senedd, and hopefully, you'll have an opportunity to raise these important issues. Let me be clear that patient safety continues to be a full priority for this Government. We expect every health board to have disease control processes in place in order to control cases effectively. I will also ensure that the Cabinet Minister is aware that you raised this issue with me today.
documents.text_cy: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r mater hwn. Dwi'n gobeithio eich bod chi hefyd wedi cymryd y cyfle i ysgrifennu at y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal. Mae yna gwestiynau i'r Gweinidog yfory yma yn y Senedd, a gobeithio y bydd yna gyfle i godi'r materion pwysig hyn. Yn sicr, gadewch i fi fod yn glir, mae diogelwch cleifion yn parhau i fod yn flaenoriaeth lwyr i'r Llywodraeth hon. Rydyn ni'n disgwyl i bob bwrdd iechyd gael trefniadau atal a rheoli heintiau cadarn ar waith i atal, adnabod a rheoli achosion yn effeithiol. Mi fyddaf i hefyd yn sicrhau bod y Gweinidog Cabinet yn ymwybodol eich bod chi wedi codi'r mater hwn efo fi heddiw.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: I'm requesting a Government statement on its tourism strategy. A strategy is not saying that tourism is important to the Welsh economy and that we want it. Which tourism sectors does the Welsh Government think are important? How are they going to target groups? How will they distinguish between day tourists and overnight tourists? I would prioritise active tourism, such as hiking, cycling and golf. The question is can we share golf tourism with Ireland. Has anybody asked? I would also prioritise cultural tourism to eisteddfods and historical buildings, including chapels and churches. But we do need a strategy.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Thank you very much to the Member. I'm pleased that you agree with me that we do need a new culture and sport strategy, which will include a focus on the economy and tourism. I would encourage every Member to engage with that consultation, which is open until 18 December. I'm looking forward greatly to receiving Mike Hedges's comments as we develop that strategy.
documents.text_cy: Diolch yn fawr iawn i'r Aelod. Dwi'n falch eich bod chi'n cytuno efo fi bod angen strategaeth ddiwylliant a chwaraeon newydd i Gymru, a fydd yn cynnwys ffocws ar yr economi a thwristiaeth. Byddwn i'n annog pob Aelod i ymwneud â'r ymgynghoriad hwnnw, sydd ar agor tan 18 Rhagfyr. Dwi'n edrych ymlaen yn fawr at dderbyn sylwadau Mike Hedges ac i'w hystyried nhw'n fanwl wrth inni ddatblygu a llunio'r strategaeth honno.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text:
Can I call for two statements today, please? The first is from the Cabinet Secretary for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy in relation to the mobile network. Action has been taken in Scotland and England, and they've announced this week in Scotland a consultation on changing permitted development rights in order to address mobile black spots. Given the essential nature of a decent mobile signal now, Wales is falling behind with this important digital infrastructure. We clearly need some action here, and I would be grateful if we could have an update on what action the Welsh Government is taking.

Also, can I call for a statement from the Welsh Government Cabinet Secretary responsible for social justice and equality on the action being taken by the Welsh Government to address antisemitism in Wales? As we all know, tomorrow marks the third anniversary of those barbaric attacks by Hamas and Islamic Jihad terrorists against Israeli citizens. All of us have condemned those attacks, and what we need to make sure is that Wales is taking appropriate action to address the rise in antisemitism that we've seen in our country since.

One positive action that the previous Welsh Government took, of course, was to recognise the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance's definition of antisemitism, and I'd be grateful if the Welsh Government could reaffirm its commitment to that definition so that we can be sure that the same action will be taken by this new Welsh Government as the previous one in terms of providing some leadership on that issue.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text:
I hope that the Member will have heard the First Minister state unambiguously earlier that we totally condemn any antisemitism. I hope that we can be united as a Senedd on that.

Also, the Deputy First Minister, in her work as Cabinet Minister for Social Justice and Equality, has been looking at the 'Anti-racist Wales Action Plan' to ensure that it is fit for purpose, reflecting on what we have seen in terms of the increase in hate of all types, including antisemitism. I will certainly raise your points with her.

In terms of your first point, clearly, digital infrastructure is crucially important; it's important for our economy. I know that this is something that the Cabinet Minister is taking seriously. I will raise the specific points that you made with him and ensure that there is an update on that work.
documents.text_cy:
Dwi'n gobeithio bod yr Aelod wedi clywed y Prif Weinidog yn gyfan gwbl ddiamwys yn gynharach o ran ein bod ni'n condemnio'n llwyr unrhyw wrthsemitiaeth. Dwi'n gobeithio ein bod ni'n unedig fel Senedd ar hynny.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Trefnydd, in a free society, we show our faces. It's how we recognise each other, it's how we trust each other, it's how we talk to each other. A nurse needs to see their patient, a teacher needs to see their parent at the school gate. For public safety, it's important. Reform's position is clear: we would ban the burqa and every other full face covering in public. Trefnydd, could we please have a statement setting out the Welsh Government's position on this? I know this matter falls outside the Senedd's powers, but if the Welsh Government will be making representations to the UK Government on Wales's behalf, it would be beneficial for this entire Senedd to understand your position on this. Also, feel free to sign our petition on this. Diolch.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: No, there will be no statement on this issue. As the Member has noted, this is an issue that is not devolved. But could I be clear, as I was in response to Darren Millar just now? This Government condemns all forms of racism, any idea that someone doesn't deserve to be able to live their life in the way that they have the right to live that life. Racism is a great problem in society now, and that's something that constituents tell us consistently. We all have a responsibility in this Chamber to ensure that we do support everyone that we represent, all members of society, and ensure that everyone feels safe, and that we all co-operate to ensure that racism doesn't continue here in Wales. There is no place for racism in Wales.
documents.text_cy: Na, fydd yna ddim datganiad ar y mater hwn. Fel mae'r Aelod wedi nodi, mae hwn yn fater sydd ddim wedi ei ddatganoli. Ond gaf i fod yn glir, fel oeddwn i yn fy ymateb i i Darren Millar rŵan? Mae'r Llywodraeth hon yn condemnio unrhyw fath o hiliaeth, unrhyw fath o roi'r syniad nad yw rhywun yn haeddu gallu byw eu bywydau yn unol â'r ffordd y maen nhw'n cael yr hawl i fyw eu bywydau. Mae hiliaeth yn rhywbeth sydd yn broblem fawr o fewn cymdeithas ar y funud. Mae hwn yn rhywbeth mae etholwyr yn ei ddweud wrthym ni yn gyson. Mae yna gyfrifoldeb ar bob un ohonon ni yn y Siambr hon i sicrhau ein bod ni yn cefnogi pawb rydyn ni'n eu cynrychioli, pob aelod o gymdeithas, a sicrhau bod pawb yn teimlo'n ddiogel, a'n bod ni i gyd yn cydweithio i sicrhau nad yw hiliaeth yn parhau yma yng Nghymru. documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text:
Minister, can I please request a statement from the Cabinet Minister for health and social care on support for people living with Huntington's disease? Huntington's is a rare neurological condition where symptoms affect thinking and cognitive abilities, as well as movement and behaviour. Symptoms usually develop between the ages of 30 and 50, with life expectancy from diagnosis being just 20 years. Anyone who has a parent with a faulty gene has a one in two chance of having Huntington's themselves. It's a really complex condition, with people requiring support from a number of health and care professionals. There's also a considerable mental health burden, with people often caring for family members whilst worrying about potentially carrying the faulty gene themselves.

Guidance published by the previous Welsh Government makes clear that those with a neurological condition such as Huntington's disease should not be excluded from mental health services. Guidance also calls for co-ordination of care across services, professions and agencies. Too many people say the healthcare service they access does not, in fact, meet their needs. A statement from the Cabinet Minister setting out what action the Welsh Government is taking to ensure that people with this devastating disease get the mental health support that they need and have a health professional to co-ordinate their care would be greatly appreciated. Thank you.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: I thank the Member for raising an issue that I'm sure a number of constituents have raised with us. I know that it's an issue that's been raised with me in casework. You will have heard me say that the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care has questions tomorrow, so there is an opportunity to raise this at that point. I would also ask the Member, if she hasn't already done so, to write to the Cabinet Minister to ensure that she gets a full response on this issue.
documents.text_cy: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi mater dwi'n siŵr mae nifer o etholwyr wedi ei godi gyda ni. Dwi'n gwybod ei fod o'n fater yn sydd wedi ei godi gyda fi drwy waith achos. Fe fyddwch chi wedi fy nghlywed i'n dweud bod gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal gwestiynau yfory, felly mae yna gyfle i godi hyn bryd hynny. Byddwn i hefyd yn gofyn i'r Aelod, os nad ydy hi eisoes wedi, ysgrifennu at y Gweinidog Cabinet i sicrhau ei bod hi'n cael ateb llawn ar y mater hwn.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Trefnydd, could I ask for a statement from the Cabinet Secretary for health and social care on the operation of the 'Listening to People' NHS complaints process? Constituents have raised concerns with me following their experience of pursuing complaints involving Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board. The new system places clear requirements on health bodies, including acknowledgement within five working days and a 10 working day early resolution stage. However, concerns have been raised with me about what happens when a patient believes that the health board itself has failed to follow those requirements. Could we therefore have a statement from the Cabinet Secretary explaining how compliance with 'Listening to People' is monitored, what action the Welsh Government can take where a health board is not compliant, and what effective route is available to a patient who believes the complaints process itself has failed? Thank you.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: I thank the Member for raising these issues. documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Prynhawn da, Drefnydd. Can I ask for a statement, please, on radical reform of services for our care-experienced young people? Back in July 2023, we debated in the Senedd the Children, Young People and Education Committee's report on this subject. Of the committee's 12 radical recommendations, the then Government accepted just one, rejecting—amongst other things—making care experience a protected characteristic and placing corporate duties on a statutory level. In that debate the now Deputy First Minister shared my disappointment that the Government then said it wasn't sufficiently bold, brave or ambitious. So, given that situation, I'd be pleased to hear from Plaid Cymru exactly how they're going to incorporate these issues around radical reform. It hasn't been so far in your statement for government or in your manifesto, but you've had a busy time, so I'm hoping that there will be a focus now on ensuring that our care-experienced young people across Wales get the services that they deserve. Diolch yn fawr iawn.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text:
I thank the Member for raising this issue. Clearly, you will be aware of Plaid Cymru's commitment in terms of what you've outlined. The Deputy Minister with responsibility for this has heard the comments that you have made this afternoon.

Removing profit from the care sector is an issue that we worked on during the co-operation agreement, and that legislation is now in place and we're moving towards implementation during this Senedd term. The previous Government did sign a statement in 2025. As a new Government, we do support the principle of creating a care system that is more focused on families, is based on rights, is trauma informed, is locally rooted and is ambitious for all children, whilst removing profit from childcare and ensuring that no young person leaves care and goes into homelessness also. I do very much hope, given the fact that you will have heard this, Deputy Minister, that there will be an opportunity for you and the Member to discuss this issue further.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text: Trefnydd, can I ask for a statement on the Government's plans for improving pre-application consultations for major energy infrastructure developments, including solar farms, windfarms, new pylons and substations? My constituents feel ignored and dismayed. They believe these applications are just tick-box exercises. They tell me that notices intended to inform them are put up in places where they cannot be seen. They say letters arrive so late they have no meaningful chance to respond. To them, it feels like they are being deliberately denied a voice in decisions that will affect their homes and communities. They say they are being treated like mushrooms: fed farmyard manure and kept in the dark. So, Trefnydd, will the Government make a statement on how it will improve pre-application consultations for major energy infrastructure developments and ensure that communities are genuinely heard? Diolch.

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text:
Thank you, Deputy Presiding Officer. I'd like to ask for a statement from the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability on how the Welsh Government intends to turn the lessons from this summer's wildfires and the very real risk of flooding this autumn and winter into investment in rural communities such as those across Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd.

Research has highlighted that measures such as rewetting peatland and better land management can help prevent wildfires, while also slowing water run-off and reducing flood risk. Indeed, the Welsh Government has already committed more than £5 million to natural flood management this financial year. So, could we have a statement setting out how farmers and landowners will be supported to deliver landscape-scale resilience and whether the Welsh Government will use this opportunity to bring much-needed investment and jobs into rural communities like mine?

documents.item: 3. Business Statement and Announcement
documents.text:

To be clear, the First Minister leads on resilience, and then individual Ministers, such as the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability, clearly have a role in terms of flooding and so on, and in terms of rural policy and farmers. So, that collaboration is important. 

There was a statement made. This was raised at that point as the work was proceeding. Of course, there will be further opportunities for Members to scrutinise, ask questions and have an input into that work.

documents.item: 4. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Transport: Strategic Priorities for the Menai Strait Crossings and M4 around Newport
documents.text: The next item is a statement by the Deputy Minister for Transport: strategic priorities for the Menai strait crossings and the M4 around Newport. I call on the Deputy Minister for Transport, Mark Hooper.
documents.text_cy: Nesaf, datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Drafnidiaeth: blaenoriaethau strategol ar gyfer croesfannau'r Fenai a'r M4 o amgylch Casnewydd. Galwaf ar y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Drafnidiaeth, Mark Hooper.

documents.item: 4. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Transport: Strategic Priorities for the Menai Strait Crossings and M4 around Newport
documents.text: Dirprwy Lywydd, today I would like to set out the next steps for the Menai crossings and the M4 around Newport. We have agreed a way forward.
documents.text_cy: Dirprwy Lywydd, heddiw hoffwn nodi’r camau nesaf ar gyfer croesfannau'r Fenai a’r M4 o amgylch Casnewydd. Rydym wedi cytuno ar y ffordd ymlaen.

documents.item: 4. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Transport: Strategic Priorities for the Menai Strait Crossings and M4 around Newport
documents.text:
The challenges on these routes are not new. They affect communities, businesses and travellers every day. The reviews we commissioned at the start of the summer were not about repeating decades of work explaining the problems, they were intended to identify a practical way forward. They have given us a clear direction. Today I am announcing action to develop a third Menai crossing and action to develop roads-based and engineering solutions for the M4 around Newport, alongside a programme of improvements that will help people and businesses while that work progresses.

Dirprwy Lywydd, people on Ynys Môn and across the north of our country know how disruptive it can be when one of the Menai crossings is restricted or closed. The review confirms that resilience remains the key challenge. That is why this Government will immediately recommence development work for a third Menai crossing. This will include design development, environmental assessment, business case preparation and the statutory processes needed to establish a deliverable scheme.

People have waited a long time for certainty about the future of the crossings. Today we are providing that direction. A third crossing remains the most effective option for improving resilience and providing additional capacity across the Menai strait. But major infrastructure cannot be delivered simply by announcing it. The necessary development work must be undertaken if we are to move from aspiration to a proposal that, ultimately, can be developed.

Alongside this work, we will continue investing in the infrastructure that we already have. We will maintain and operate both existing crossings to keep them safe and reliable. We will continue investment in targeted resilience measures on Britannia bridge, including wind deflectors, variable speed limits and other operational improvements designed to reduce disruption and keep traffic moving during challenging conditions. These measures will not replace the need for a third crossing. They will help improve resilience while development work on the third crossing progresses.

The review also examined three-lane tidal flow operation on Britannia bridge. The evidence identified significant safety and operational concerns and does not support taking this option forward.

Dirprwy Lywydd, turning now to the M4 around Newport: this is one of the most important transport corridors in Wales. Every day, thousands of people and businesses rely on this route to get to work, move goods and connect with customers, communities and ports across Wales. Yet, congestion continues to cause unreliable journeys and disruption that can quickly spread across the wider network. The review is clear that doing nothing is not an option. It also shows there is no single short-term intervention capable of solving the problem on its own. That is why this Welsh Government will now begin an 18-month programme of work to develop roads-based and engineering solutions for the M4 around Newport. This programme will consider a range of roads-based and engineering interventions and will identify a preferred option capable of providing a long-term response to the challenges on this route.

documents.item: 4. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Transport: Strategic Priorities for the Menai Strait Crossings and M4 around Newport
documents.text:
Many people will understandably say that this issue has been debated for decades. They are right. But this work is not about revisiting old arguments. It is about developing options against current policy, environmental requirements, planning considerations and future travel demands, so that decisions can be taken on the basis of robust evidence and a clear understanding of what can realistically be delivered. Our objective is straightforward: we need a solution that is affordable, deliverable and capable of attracting the support and investment needed to make it happen. Without undertaking this work, there can be no credible pathway towards delivering future roads-based and engineering solutions.

But while this work progresses, we cannot simply wait. That is why we are also announcing a programme of improvements over the next five years. We will invest in the maintenance and renewal of the existing motorway and strategic road network. Over many years, Governments have often faced a choice between accepting disruption now or delaying important work until later. Understandably, there has often been a desire to minimise disruption in the short term, but that can make long-term challenges harder to address. Key infrastructure now requires significant renewal and maintenance work. I want to be honest: there will be periods of disruption while this work takes place. Nobody wants roadworks. Nobody enjoys delays. But continuing to defer this work will only lead to greater disruption and cost in the future. This Government is choosing to deal with that problem now.

We will also implement a five-year delivery plan, focused on practical improvements that people will start to see over the next two to three years, with further benefits building over time. This will include improvements to the way the motorway is operated and managed, including targeted improvements to roads and junctions, including potential closures, in and around Newport to improve traffic flow and resilience. The review found that measures such as these offer some of the quickest opportunities to improve traffic flow and resilience in the M4.

But we also recognise that changes affecting the motorway can have consequences for local roads. We will therefore work closely with Newport City Council, local communities and Members to develop these interventions so that the local impacts are properly considered alongside the benefits to the M4. At the same time, we will introduce measures to improve freight resilience by making better use of alternative routes such as the A465. This will maximise the investment made in the A465, supporting the provision of facilities that HGV drivers deserve, and at the same time alleviating pressure on the M4.

We will also continue investing in public transport, making it easier for more people to choose rail and bus services for everyday journeys between Newport and Cardiff, across the wider M4 corridor, and onwards into the rest of Wales and into England. The UK Government has committed to funding the rail stations recommended by the South East Wales Transport Commission. Last week I attended the joint UK-Welsh Government Wales rail board to discuss how we can accelerate delivery. I am pleased that Network Rail have committed to work collaboratively with Transport for Wales to draw on the expertise of both organisations, and TfW will take a direct role in constructing the stations.

We are setting up a new network south-east Wales board to oversee delivery. I have asked the team to prioritise delivery of the Cardiff parkway and Magor and Undy stations, so that communities can begin to benefit from these investments as soon as possible. We will also seek to improve access to Severn Tunnel Junction railway station and support improvements to bus connectivity between Newport and Cardiff, giving real options for travellers.

Dirprwy Lywydd, for too long, people and businesses have seen congestion around Newport become an accepted part of everyday life. This Government is choosing to act. The programme we are taking forward could reduce peak-hour traffic by about one in 10 vehicles. On a motorway that is already operating at or above capacity at the busiest times, that matters. It is a meaningful improvement over doing nothing and simply accepting increasing congestion on the network. But what matters is what these improvements mean in practice for people using the network every day. It means better travel choices through improved rail and bus services. It means the network is better able to cope when incidents occur, reducing the risk of small problems becoming major disruption. These are practical improvements that people should begin to notice in their everyday lives over the coming years.

Dirprwy Lywydd, people want action, not endless discussion. They want government to deal with today's challenges while properly planning for the future. That is exactly what we are doing. At the Menai strait, we are getting on with the work needed to develop a third crossing whilst managing resilience now. Around Newport, we are developing long-term road space and engineering solutions for the M4 whilst delivering practical improvements over the next five years. These are major transport challenges that have built up over many years; they will not be resolved overnight. But, today, we are providing a clear direction, taking practical actions now and developing the longer-term solutions needed for the future.

documents.item: 4. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Transport: Strategic Priorities for the Menai Strait Crossings and M4 around Newport
documents.text: Dirprwy Lywydd, we are taking action now. We are delivering improvements over the next five years and developing solutions for the future. Thank you.
documents.text_cy: Ddirprwy Lywydd, rydym yn gweithredu nawr. Rydym yn cyflawni gwelliannau dros y bum mlynedd nesaf ac yn datblygu atebion ar gyfer ein dyfodol. Diolch yn fawr.

documents.item: 4. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Transport: Strategic Priorities for the Menai Strait Crossings and M4 around Newport
documents.text:
Oh dear, oh dear, oh dear, Minister. We were expecting a lot more on this side of the Chamber. But, anyway, we'll start north and then we'll travel south, if that's okay.

So, I'll start with the positives. Nice to see we're doing some baby steps with the current bridges that cross the Menai strait. Wind deflectors—let's get on with that as soon as we can, improve those; we've got a winter ahead of us. And varying the speed limit—we like varying the speed limit in this Chamber, don't we—I'll give you a positive on that one. But, in terms of the actual third bridge, it sounds like you're just thinking about a third bridge, which simply is not good enough. So, you're going to recommence development work and look at design development, environmental assessment, business case preparation. To me, it doesn't sound like you're completely committed to a third crossing, because I thought we'd done all this work before. I thought this was called the purple route and that that work had been done. And obviously what's disappointing to see, and this is why I question your commitment, is there's nothing in here about funding a third bridge. It's going to be an expensive project and is going to need cross-party support, and there's nothing in here about that. So, I want to ask you, and you can answer once I've finished, clearly: are you actually committed to building the third bridge across the Menai strait, 'yes' or 'no'?

Right, then, let's head down south. Now you need more thinking time—18 months of more thinking time—about solutions. And again, I thought we'd been here and gone through all of that with the M4 relief road and the black route. And in between the thinking time—which you clearly need, fair enough—for the next five years, you're going to do some improvements, which, personally, I think is just a sticking-plaster approach that ties in directly to Plaid Cymru's anti-motorist stance.

Let's talk about closing junctions. I do love the statistic about one in 10 cars not making it onto the M4. Of course they can't make it onto the M4, because they can't get onto the M4 because you've closed the junction. Closing junctions doesn't solve congestion and it's going to move that onto Newport's local roads. Newport City Council recently—July 2026—voted unanimously against any measure that diverts traffic onto Newport's already congested streets. I don't think they will be so delighted with your statement today. As we in Reform have said, stopping cars getting onto the motorway isn't a solution that Newport will thank you for. And in your own assessment, the cost of this is £14 million, and reducing traffic by a whopping 3 per cent.

Let's go over to the Heads of the Valleys plan. So, let me just get this right: ferries transport comes off the boats in Pembroke and then goes across east to Dover and on to Europe, and what you want to do is encourage, persuade, divert that freight traffic to go up over the Heads of the Valleys and back down again, and the cost of doing that is £49 million, which is some pretty swanky cafes and some nice rest facilities, and you think that will reduce the traffic on the M4 by 1 per cent. It's just not going to happen.

And then, finally, we get on to rail. Now, let's be clear: Reform supports more rail capacity, but rail should add choice, not be used to justify restricting road access. As Laura Anne Jones pointed out, the M4 users have no realistic alternative. We need to remind ourselves that, unlike us, there are a lot of people who aren't members of the lanyard class who go to work each day with a small briefcase. How are delivery drivers and tradespeople going to get on the train? 'Excuse me, ma'am, can you just move to one side while I put my 12 pots of paint and my toolbox there?' It's not going to happen.

Basically, Minister, I'm asking you to drop your ideology. What you've done here is pretend to be committed to fixing the road issues, but actually you're thinking about a bridge, you've got 18 months more of thinking about the M4, and you've got a five-year scheme, which, essentially, is going to cost millions of pounds and reduce traffic congestion by 4 per cent. So, here is the solution. On your last page of your statement, you say, 'We are developing a long-term roads-based and engineering solution.' Well, I'll tell you, we've got one: it's the M4 relief road, the black route. Reform UK have costed this at £2.8 billion. Yes, that's a lot of money, but I will guarantee here that, if there is a Reform Welsh Government, we will be lobbying and working with a Reform UK Westminster Government—which is coming, ladies and gentlemen—and we will build the M4 relief road. So, Minister, I want to confirm: are you committed to the bridge, completely and utterly committed? And please stop thinking and just get on with it. Diolch yn fawr.

documents.item: 4. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Transport: Strategic Priorities for the Menai Strait Crossings and M4 around Newport
documents.text:
Thank you for the question. Before I answer, I just want to thank those Members who turned up for the briefing with officials this morning, and also subsequent conversations in this regard. It was a shame that Members from Reform chose not to undertake those conversations. There were specific conversations that were not entered into, and that was a real shame, because that would have given them the chance to have understood some of the detail behind this more clearly.

In answer to the questions on Menai, I don't think the Member, frankly, understands the process you need to go through to build. This is a significant piece of engineering. It is appropriate that we do it in the phases that we say we are. To be clear, this Government is committed to delivering a third crossing across the Menai. There are no ifs, no buts. That is absolutely clear. What you have to do to do that is to take stages. Now, the Member, and all of this group around here, just seem to think that you can click a finger and things happen. Let's get into the real world. The real world is that it takes real work to get these things done. The interesting thing is, when I was speaking to civil servants earlier prior to this, I was saying I was looking forward to this debate, because I do look forward to these debates. Do you know what they were saying? They're looking forward to getting stuck in to doing the work. That's what they're waiting for, and that's what's going to happen. What's happened for too long is this body politic has failed to deliver. If we have conversations that are in the style that we've had today, we'll continue to do that. But the rest of the Siambr, hopefully, will focus on getting things done. Because if you're just going to backbite on that, it helps nobody, frankly.

Turning to the M4, I think this is a real misunderstanding as well of what a 10 per cent change will do on the M4 with the plan of action that we've put together. Ten per cent—. And I'm sure that Members opposite me as well are probably thinking, 'I wish we'd done some more of this 10 per cent.' But, over the past 27 years, there's been very limited change on the M4. This Government is committing itself, over the next five years, to making an actual difference to people. And 3 per cent here and 1 per cent there makes a real difference. This is about a strategic suite of projects that need to be deployed together. These are the ways that we make the difference to the M4. And it's not straightforward. There is no silver bullet. If there was, we'd talk about it. You talk about the black route as if it's deliverable. That went when it was cancelled. The protected route status went when it was cancelled. So, we're talking about decades of work to even get that off the ground. So, to suggest to the people outside that you can deliver it in an instant is disingenuous—and I'm being kind in saying that.

In terms of the A465—. There are a lot of questions to get through, I will try and be—. But, in terms of the A465, unlike you I've actually spoken to hauliers, who see this as a realistic option. But the haulage companies are looking for facilities, because, unlike some parts of Europe where they actually invest in facilities for drivers—. Drivers are professional. Across the UK, we have very, very poor facilities. This Government is going to make a difference to that, and we've had support from across the industry to say that they want to see those facilities. That will direct people across the piece, and that's including people from Ireland as well as haulage companies from the UK.

Rail adding choice and taking people off the motorway—. One of the things about adding choice using rail is exactly what you just said, it takes people—. So, I may be taking a car; I can now use the rail. That frees up space on the motorway for those people who need to use the motorway in the way that you described. It's a practical way of making a difference. The sad thing is that the Burns review—. I can just hear muttering behind me. Do you want to make an intervention or not?

documents.item: 4. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Transport: Strategic Priorities for the Menai Strait Crossings and M4 around Newport
documents.text:
Making room for others who are using that road system by putting them on the railways is an important thing. The Burns review reported six and a half, almost seven years ago. I think the disappointment is that nothing's happened in that time. But what has been good—. And listening to the Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution earlier, he described the positive conversations we've been having with UK Government. That's the same for this. We've had a continued commitment from the UK Government to the £14 billion. The Prime Minister has made it. The Secretary of State has made it. The point now is to get that transferred in, in this current spending review, so we can start to move on those stations. We've identified the ones we want to move quickly on, and we will do.

I'm just going to—. The point about ideology is, frankly, ludicrous, ultimately. All we've heard is 'ideology'. The suggestion that we're taking these things, that we're not dealing with cars, helping people to move faster on the motorway through cars, which is exactly what this statement is, which is exactly what we're talking about now, is frankly ludicrous. We need to move together as a body politic and start delivering these things and stop this calling for—. It's just—. We're not dealing with the issues. We're not dealing with the issues at hand.

documents.item: 4. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Transport: Strategic Priorities for the Menai Strait Crossings and M4 around Newport
documents.text:
I thank the Deputy Minister for his statement. After 30 talking shops, reviews and expert panels in the Government's first 100 days, I was hoping for something different from you today. I'm sorry to say I've been rather disappointed.

Now, progress on that third Menai crossing is very welcome. It builds on the work that Welsh Labour had undertaken in Government. But families in Newport will feel let down that, rather than acting now, the Government is launching yet another review on the M4, and we won't have any answers for 18 months. So, my first question to you today, Minister, is: why will it take that long to come up with some serious road-based answers for traffic around Newport? Aren't you just kicking the can down the road and hoping that families in Newport won't notice? And Deputy Minister, if you'd spoken to people in Newport, we think you wouldn't need that long. You'd have been told unequivocally that junction closures will bring more traffic and more air pollution, that silent killer, into the hearts and lungs of communities.

In Government, Welsh Labour took action to help alleviate congestion on the M4 around Newport. We'd secured funding for new railway stations from the UK Labour Government as part of that generational £14 billion commitment to transform rail infrastructure in Wales. We completed the Heads of the Valleys A465 road, the biggest road building scheme in Europe, offering traffic from the north and Midlands an alternative route into south Wales. So, I do welcome your proposals to increase the level of haulage traffic there.

We also commissioned independent evidence-based resilience studies, not just of the M4, but the A55, the A494 and the A483 to ensure that roads are fit for the future. Those resilience studies are vital work that should form the basis of future recommendations, but they appear now to be gathering dust on the Government's shelves, with no comment today on the A484 or the A483 or the A55 east of the Menai strait, where you'll know that there are significant traffic problems. Deputy Minister, as you know, Welsh Labour's view is that devolution shouldn't stop at Cardiff Bay, that Wales is too centralised, and local leaders should have a far greater say on the issues that affect their communities, and this decision today is a case in point: trunk roads are maintained and owned by the Welsh Government, but they should be designed and delivered for the regions and economies that they serve. So, will you commit to engaging fully with families, drivers, businesses and local leaders in Newport before any decision is taken about junction closures? Will you also commit to publishing the evidence behind any junction closures in full? And finally, will you also commit the Government to publishing a full response to those resilience reviews that Welsh Labour started in Government?
